questions.question: Who won the Men's Singles tennis gold medal at Roland Garros in August 2026, completing the Career Golden Slam?

questions.question: Which nation won the Men's Basketball gold medal in August 2026, defeating host nation France in the final?

questions.question: Who was named the MVP of the Men's Olympic Basketball Tournament in August 2026?

questions.question: Who won the Men's Singles title at the Cincinnati Masters tennis tournament in August 2026?

questions.question: Who won the Women's Singles title at the Cincinnati Open in August 2026?

questions.question: Which European football club won the UEFA Super Cup in Warsaw in August 2026?

questions.question: Who won the Dutch Grand Prix Formula 1 race at Zandvoort in August 2026?

questions.question: Which Indian athlete won gold in the Men's High Jump at the World U20 Athletics Championships in Lima in August 2026?

questions.question: Who was named the head coach of India's junior men's hockey team in August 2026?

questions.question: Which Indian grandmaster won the 2026 Biel Chess Festival Grandmaster Triathlon?

questions.question: Which Indian women's table tennis player reached the Top 25 of the ITTF World Rankings in August 2026?

questions.question: Which stadium was officially chosen to host the final of the 2026 ICC Women's T20 World Cup?

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution of India did the President address both Houses of Parliament assembled together at the commencement of the Budget Session?

questions.question: Which state assembly passed the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill in February, becoming the first state in independent India to do so?
questions.explanation: The Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly passed the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill 2024/2026, making it the first state in independent India to formulate and pass a UCC legislation.

questions.question: Who chaired the High-Level Committee on 'One Nation, One Election' which submitted its comprehensive recommendations to the President of India?
questions.explanation: Former President of India Ram Nath Kovind chaired the 8-member High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act is known as 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam' reserving one-third of seats for women in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?
questions.explanation: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023 provides 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, the Legislative Assembly of NCT of Delhi, and all State Legislative Assemblies.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India in February 2026 exercised its extraordinary plenary powers under which Article to declare the result of the Chandigarh Mayoral Election?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court invoked Article 142 ('Enforcement of decrees and orders of Supreme Court and orders as to discovery, etc.') to ensure complete justice and uphold democratic purity.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the 'Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana' (PM-MKSSY) approved by the Union Cabinet?
options: Formalization of the fisheries sector and microenterprise credit support
questions.explanation: PM-MKSSY is a central sub-scheme under PMMSY focused on formalizing the unorganized fisheries sector, supporting micro & small enterprises, and facilitating credit.

questions.question: Which portal was launched by the Ministry of Electronics and IT to facilitate citizen grievance appeals against decisions of social media Grievance Officers?
questions.explanation: The Digital India GAC portal enables users dissatisfied with platform grievance officer resolutions to appeal online seamlessly.

questions.question: The Law Commission of India is currently headed by which retired Chief Justice / Judge as its Chairperson?
questions.explanation: Justice Ritu Raj Awasthi (former Chief Justice of Karnataka High Court) chaired the 22nd Law Commission of India before joining Lokpal.

questions.question: Which Union Ministry launched the 'Mera Pehla Vote Desh Ke Liye' nation-wide voter awareness campaign?
options: Ministry of Education and Ministry of I&B
questions.explanation: The campaign was spearheaded by the Ministry of Education in collaboration with the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting and the Election Commission of India to engage first-time voters.

questions.question: Under the SVAMITVA scheme, which technology is primarily used for surveying rural inhabited areas?
questions.explanation: The SVAMITVA scheme utilizes drone technology for mapping land parcels in rural inhabited areas (Abadi) to issue legal property cards.

questions.question: What is the name of the central scheme that provides financial assistance of ₹6,000 per year in three equal installments to eligible farmer families?
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) provides ₹6,000 annually directly into the bank accounts of landholding farmer families via DBT.

questions.question: Which constitutional body is responsible for delimitation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies under Article 82 of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Under Article 82, Parliament enacts a Delimitation Act after every census, establishing a high-powered Delimitation Commission whose orders cannot be challenged in any court.

questions.question: In the context of Indian governance, what does 'CVIGIL' app developed by the Election Commission of India allow citizens to do?
options: Report Model Code of Conduct and election expenditure violations in real time
questions.explanation: cVIGIL allows citizens to upload geotagged photographs or audio-video clips of Model Code of Conduct (MCC) and expenditure violations with guaranteed fast investigation within 100 minutes.

questions.question: Which Union Territory recently held discussions regarding constitutional safeguards under the Sixth Schedule or Article 371?

questions.question: What is the term of office for a Member of the Rajya Sabha as per the Constitution and Representation of the People Act, 1951?
questions.explanation: While Rajya Sabha is a permanent body not subject to dissolution, one-third of its members retire every second year, giving individual members a 6-year term.

questions.question: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha as per Article 64 of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Article 64 specifies that the Vice-President shall be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

questions.question: Which state government notified the implementation of the 'Panchayat Extension to Scheduled Areas' (PESA) rules in February 2026?
questions.explanation: Several fifth schedule states including Jharkhand have notified state PESA rules to empower Gram Sabhas in tribal areas.

questions.question: What is the quorum required to constitute a sitting of either House of Parliament as per Article 100(3)?
options: One-tenth of the total number of members
One-sixth of the total number of members
One-fourth of the total number of members
One-twelfth of the total number of members
questions.explanation: Article 100(3) states that until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House is one-tenth of the total number of members.

questions.question: Which Ministry implements the 'Vibrant Villages Programme' covering border blocks along the northern frontier?
questions.explanation: The Centrally Sponsored 'Vibrant Villages Programme' is implemented by the Ministry of Home Affairs to comprehensively develop border villages along northern borders.

questions.question: Under which constitutional provision can the President grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment?
questions.explanation: Article 72 empowers the President of India to grant pardons and suspend, remit, or commute sentences in all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death or under union laws.

questions.question: Which portal was established by the Government of India as a unified portal for citizen-centric digital safety to report lost or stolen mobile phones?

questions.question: What is the maximum permissible strength of the Council of Ministers in a State Assembly under Article 164(1A)?

questions.explanation: Introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act 2003, Article 164(1A) limits the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of the total assembly strength (minimum 12 ministers).

questions.question: Which High Court recently celebrated its diamond jubilee / sesquicentennial milestone with a digital repository launch?

questions.question: What is the nodal agency for the implementation of the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) and Digital India initiatives?

questions.question: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha)?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule to the Indian Constitution details the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to each State and Union Territory.

questions.question: The Central Government notified the Citizenship Amendment Rules, 2024 to implement the CAA 2019 in March. Persons from how many minority communities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan are eligible under it?

questions.explanation: The CAA facilitates citizenship for 6 persecuted minority communities (Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians) from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who arrived in India on or before December 31, 2014.

questions.question: What was the cutoff date specified under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2019 for entry into India?

questions.question: A Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court of India struck down the Electoral Bonds Scheme as unconstitutional, citing violation of which fundamental right?

questions.question: Which bank was directed by the Supreme Court to disclose all data regarding purchases and redemptions of Electoral Bonds?

questions.question: How many phases were announced by the Election Commission of India for the 18th General Elections to the Lok Sabha in March 2026?

questions.question: What is the minimum age prescribed under Article 84 of the Constitution for a person to be eligible for election as a member of the Lok Sabha?

questions.question: Which mobile application was promoted by the Election Commission of India to help voters check their name in electoral rolls, polling station details, and digital voter slips?
questions.explanation: The Voter Helpline App is the flagship mobile app of ECI enabling voters to search names, download digital voter slips, and submit registration forms.

questions.question: Which initiative was approved by the Union Cabinet to install rooftop solar panels for 1 crore households with a financial outlay of ₹75,021 crore?

questions.question: The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) comes into operation immediately upon which event?
options: Announcement of the election schedule by the Election Commission
Issue of formal election notification by the President/Governor

questions.question: Which state became the second after Bihar to conduct and release findings of a comprehensive socio-economic and educational caste survey?

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the 'Subhadra Yojana' approved by the Odisha Government?
options: Financial voucher assistance of ₹50,000 to women over five years

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 324 of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls and conduct of all elections to Parliament and State Legislatures in the Election Commission.

questions.question: What is the statutory spending limit for candidates contesting in major Parliamentary (Lok Sabha) constituencies as revised by the Government?

questions.question: Which Commission under Article 280 recommends the distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and the States?

questions.question: Who is the Chairman of the 16th Finance Commission of India?

questions.question: What is the tenure of the 16th Finance Commission to cover recommendations for devolution of taxes?

questions.question: Which constitutional Article empowers the Supreme Court of India with original jurisdiction to decide disputes between the Union and one or more States?

questions.question: The Government of India extended the ban on which organization under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) in March 2026?

questions.question: Which state launched the 'Indiramma Indlu' housing scheme in March to provide ₹5 lakh financial assistance for building houses?

questions.question: Who heads the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) in India as its ex-officio Chairperson?

questions.question: What is the minimum percentage of VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) paper slips mandatorily counted in each assembly segment under ECI guidelines?

questions.question: Which app was launched by ECI to enable candidates and political parties to seek permissions for rallies, meetings, and vehicles online?

questions.question: Which portal facilitates the casting of Postal Ballot votes by Service Voters and Indian diplomats posted abroad?

questions.question: What does Article 326 of the Constitution of India guarantee?

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act lowered the voting age in India from 21 years to 18 years?

questions.question: On which date is National Panchayati Raj Day celebrated across India every year?

questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added which Part to the Constitution of India?

questions.question: How many functional matters are listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution for Panchayats?

questions.question: The Supreme Court in April 2026 rejected the plea for 100% cross-verification of EVM votes with VVPAT slips in which landmark case?

Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain
People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India
T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
questions.explanation: The two-judge bench of the Supreme Court held that the existing EVM-VVPAT architecture is robust, tamper-proof, and upholds electoral integrity.

questions.question: Civil Services Day is celebrated in India every year on which date?

questions.question: Which portal was launched by the Central Government to track and ensure real-time reporting of heatwave conditions across districts?

questions.question: Which Ministry issues the Model Guidelines for prevention of misleading advertisements in the coaching sector?

questions.question: What is the primary role of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) established under the NGT Act 2010?

questions.question: Where is the principal bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) located?

questions.question: Which constitutional body prepares the Annual Report on the condition of Scheduled Castes under Article 338?

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution is the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) established?

questions.question: Which constitutional body was granted constitutional status by the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018?
options: National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) under Article 338-B
questions.explanation: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act conferred constitutional status on the National Commission for Backward Classes by inserting Article 338-B.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)?
questions.explanation: Article 315 provides for the creation of a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State.

questions.question: Who appoints the Chairman and other members of the Union Public Service Commission?
questions.explanation: Under Article 316, the Chairman and other members of the UPSC are appointed by the President of India for a term of 6 years or until age 65.

questions.question: What is the tenure of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) under Article 148?
options: 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
questions.explanation: The CAG of India holds office for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever occurs first, as per Section 3 of the CAG's Act, 1971.

questions.question: Which Parliamentary Committee examines the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)?
questions.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee, consisting of 22 members (15 from Lok Sabha, 7 from Rajya Sabha), scrutinizes the annual audit reports of the CAG.

questions.question: Who is conventionally appointed as the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC)?
options: A member of the Opposition party in Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: By established parliamentary convention since 1967, the Chairperson of the PAC is selected by the Speaker from the Opposition in Lok Sabha.

questions.question: How many members does the Estimates Committee of Parliament have, and from which House are they elected?
questions.explanation: The Estimates Committee is the largest parliamentary committee with 30 members, all elected solely from the Lok Sabha for a one-year term.

questions.question: What is the minimum strength of a recognized Opposition party in Lok Sabha to claim the status of Leader of the Opposition?
options: At least 10% of the total strength of the House (55 members)
questions.explanation: To be recognized as the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, a party must secure at least 10% of the total strength of the House (i.e. 55 seats).

questions.question: Which portal was developed by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj to deliver online accounting, planning, and progress reporting for Gram Panchayats?
questions.explanation: e-GramSwaraj provides a single unified digital interface for work-based accounting and monitoring across all Gram Panchayats in India.

questions.question: What is 'Gram Manchitra' launched by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj?
options: A Spatial Planning Application using geo-spatial technology to assist Gram Panchayats in developmental planning
questions.explanation: Gram Manchitra is a Geographic Information System (GIS) application that facilitates spatial planning for Gram Panchayat development plans.

questions.question: Under Article 21-A of the Constitution, education is a fundamental right for children of which age group?
questions.explanation: Article 21-A, inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002, directs the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.

questions.question: The 'Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act' came into force on which date?
questions.explanation: The historic RTE Act enacted in 2009 came into nationwide effect on April 1, 2010 across the country.

questions.question: Which statutory authority registers and monitors political parties in India under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
questions.explanation: Under Section 29A of the RPA 1951, associations seeking recognition as political parties must submit applications for registration to the ECI.

questions.question: What is the threshold national vote share or seat requirement for a party to be recognized as a 'National Party' in India by the ECI?
options: Recognized as a State party in at least four states
Winning 10 Lok Sabha seats from one state
Winning 25% of total Rajya Sabha seats
questions.explanation: As per the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, one of the primary criteria to be recognized as a National Party is recognition as a State party in at least 4 states.

questions.question: The Central Government notified amendments to the IT Rules regarding synthetic media. What is mandatory for platforms regarding AI-generated deepfakes?
options: Visible labels/watermarks indicating artificially generated content
Total ban on all AI image generation
questions.explanation: MeitY issued advisories mandating intermediaries to prominently label or watermark synthetically generated or modified audio-visual media and inform users of legal penalties.

questions.question: Which initiative under Digital India provides real-time multi-language AI translation for public welfare portals and speeches?
questions.explanation: Digital India Bhashini enables cross-lingual AI speech-to-text, translation, and text-to-speech across 22 scheduled Indian languages.

questions.question: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the NITI Aayog?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog).

questions.question: Who is the current Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog?
questions.explanation: Eminent economist Suman Bery was appointed Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog in May 2022 and continues to lead its policy frameworks.

questions.question: Who is the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NITI Aayog?
questions.explanation: Former Commerce Secretary B.V.R. Subrahmanyam serves as the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog.

questions.question: Under Article 75(3) of the Constitution of India, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
options: The House of the People (Lok Sabha)
questions.explanation: Article 75(3) unambiguously states that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

questions.question: What is the maximum period of time an individual can serve as a Union Minister without being elected to either House of Parliament?
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(5), a Minister who for any period of six consecutive months is not a member of either House of Parliament shall cease to be a Minister.

questions.question: Which Commission was set up under Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi to review Centre-State relations?
questions.explanation: The Punchhi Commission was constituted in 2007 and submitted its report in 2010 on structural aspects of Centre-State fiscal and political balance.

questions.question: Which landmark Supreme Court judgment in 1994 laid down stringent guidelines against the arbitrary imposition of President's Rule under Article 356?
options: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
questions.explanation: In S.R. Bommai (1994), a 9-judge bench ruled that the power under Article 356 is conditional, subject to judicial review, and floor tests must be the sole forum for testing majority.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution can a High Court issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose?
questions.explanation: Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue directions, orders, or writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, certiorar) for fundamental rights and other legal rights.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution is referred to as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar declared Article 32 as the very soul and heart of the Constitution as it provides an effective remedy against violation of fundamental rights directly before the Supreme Court.

questions.question: How many types of prerogative writs can be issued by the Supreme Court under Article 32 and High Courts under Article 226?
options: 5 writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo-Warranto)
questions.explanation: Both the Supreme Court and High Courts are empowered to issue five classic writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto.

questions.question: Which writ literally means 'We Command' in Latin and is issued to compel a public official to perform a mandatory statutory duty?
questions.explanation: Mandamus is a judicial command issued to a public authority or lower court directing the performance of a public or statutory duty that they have refused to perform.

questions.question: Which writ is issued to produce a detained person before the court to examine the lawfulness of their detention?
questions.explanation: Habeas Corpus (meaning 'You shall have the body') protects personal liberty against arbitrary and illegal detention by the State or private individuals.

questions.question: What does the writ of 'Quo-Warranto' seek to inquire into?
options: The legality of a person's claim to a public office
Transfer of a case from a lower court
questions.explanation: Quo-Warranto ('By what authority?') prevents illegal usurpation of a public office by an individual not qualified to hold it.

questions.question: Which Union Ministry oversees the implementation of the 'Mission Amrit Sarovar' aiming to develop 75 water bodies in each district?
questions.explanation: Mission Amrit Sarovar was launched as part of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav by the Ministry of Rural Development in coordination with Jal Shakti and Panchayati Raj.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the 'Pradhan Mantri Janman' (PM-JANMAN) package approved with ₹24,104 crore outlay?
options: Comprehensive socio-economic development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)
Free bus transport for urban workers
questions.explanation: PM-JANMAN targets 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) living in 18 states and UTs, delivering road connectivity, housing, clean water, and solar electrification.

questions.question: How many tribal communities in India are officially categorized as Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)?
questions.explanation: The Dhebar Commission (1973) created Primitive Tribal Groups; currently, 75 communities across 18 states and the Union Territory of Andaman & Nicobar are categorized as PVTGs.

questions.question: Which state has the highest number of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in India?
questions.explanation: Odisha is home to the largest number of PVTG communities (13 out of 75), including Bondo, Dongria Kondh, and Kutia Kondh.

questions.question: What is the official motto inscribed below the National Emblem of India on the Lion Capital of Ashoka?
questions.explanation: The words 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth Alone Triumphs) from the Mundaka Upanishad are inscribed in Devanagari script beneath the abacus of the state emblem.

questions.question: From which ancient Upanishad is the national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' taken?
questions.explanation: The profound aphorism 'Satyameva Jayate' is derived from Mantra 3.1.6 of the Mundaka Upanishad.

questions.question: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was appointed Chairman of the seven-member Drafting Committee on August 29, 1947, to prepare the draft constitution.

questions.question: Who served as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Sir B.N. Rau served as the Constitutional Advisor and prepared the initial draft of the Constitution after comparative research of global constitutions.

questions.question: The Preamble to the Constitution of India was based on which historic resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic 'Objective Resolution' on December 13, 1946, which was unanimously adopted on January 22, 1947, and formed the preamble.

questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment were the words 'SOCIALIST', 'SECULAR', and 'INTEGRITY' added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 amended the Preamble for the first and only time, adding 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'and Integrity'.

questions.question: Who took oath as the Prime Minister of India for a historic third consecutive term in June 2026?
questions.explanation: Narendra Modi was sworn in as Prime Minister of India for a third consecutive term by President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan, equalling Jawaharlal Nehru's feat.

questions.question: Who was elected as the Speaker of the 18th Lok Sabha in June 2026?
questions.explanation: Om Birla was re-elected as the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, becoming only the second person after Balram Jakhar to complete a full 5-year term and return as Speaker.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Pro-tem Speaker of the 18th Lok Sabha to administer oaths to newly elected MPs?
questions.explanation: Senior parliamentarian Bhartruhari Mahtab was appointed by the President as the Pro-tem Speaker under Article 95(1) of the Constitution.

questions.question: Who was recognized as the Leader of the Opposition in the 18th Lok Sabha, filling a post that was vacant for 10 years?
questions.explanation: Rahul Gandhi was appointed and officially recognized as the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha after the Congress party secured more than 10% of the seats.

questions.question: What was the global theme for the 10th International Day of Yoga celebrated on June 21, 2026?
questions.explanation: The theme for the 10th International Day of Yoga was 'Yoga for Self and Society', highlighting yoga's dual role in personal well-being and social cohesion.

questions.question: In which city did Prime Minister Narendra Modi lead the national International Day of Yoga celebrations on June 21, 2026?
questions.explanation: The main national Yoga Day celebration was led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Sher-i-Kashmir International Conference Centre (SKICC) on Dal Lake in Srinagar.

questions.question: In its very first cabinet meeting, the newly formed Union Cabinet approved financial assistance for how many additional houses under PMAY?
options: 3 crore houses (2 crore rural, 1 crore urban)
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved assistance to construct 3 crore additional rural and urban houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY).

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi signed his first file upon assuming office for the 3rd term authorizing which disbursement?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister signed the release of the 17th installment of the PM-KISAN scheme, transferring roughly ₹20,000 crore to 9.26 crore farmers.

questions.question: The newly constructed Nalanda University campus in Rajgir, Bihar was formally inaugurated by Prime Minister Modi in June 2026. Who was the founding chancellor of modern Nalanda University?
questions.explanation: Nobel Laureate Prof. Amartya Sen served as the first Chancellor of the revived Nalanda University, conceptualized by Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution does the President administer the oath of office and secrecy to the Prime Minister and Union Ministers?
options: Article 75(4) read with the Third Schedule
questions.explanation: Article 75(4) mandates that before a Minister enters upon his office, the President shall administer to him the oaths of office and secrecy according to forms set out in the Third Schedule.

questions.question: Which Union Minister was allocated the portfolio of Minister of Cooperation in addition to the Ministry of Home Affairs in the new Union Cabinet?
questions.explanation: Amit Shah retained both crucial portfolios—the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Cooperation.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare as well as Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers?
questions.explanation: BJP National President Jagat Prakash Nadda was inducted into the Union Cabinet as the Minister of Health & Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers.

questions.question: Who was allocated the portfolios of Ministry of Information & Broadcasting and Ministry of Railways in the Union Cabinet?
questions.explanation: Ashwini Vaishnaw was given charge of the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, along with retaining the Ministry of Railways and MeitY.

questions.question: Which former Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh was appointed as the Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development?
questions.explanation: Four-time Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan was entrusted with Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development portfolios.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways in the new Cabinet?
questions.explanation: Nitin Gadkari continued in his pivotal role heading the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for a third consecutive term.

questions.question: Which former Chief Minister of Haryana was appointed as the Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs and Minister of Power?
questions.explanation: Former Haryana Chief Minister Manohar Lal Khattar was appointed as the Minister of Housing & Urban Affairs and Minister of Power.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of days a State Legislative Assembly or Parliament can adjourn without meeting before Article 85/174 is violated?
questions.explanation: Articles 85(1) and 174(1) mandate that six months shall not intervene between the last sitting of Parliament/Assembly in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.

questions.question: Which Parliamentary procedure is used to draw the attention of the House to an urgent matter of public importance with the consent of the Speaker?
questions.explanation: A Calling Attention Notice enables an MP to call the attention of a Minister to an urgent matter of public importance with the Speaker's prior permission.

questions.question: What does 'Zero Hour' in Indian parliamentary proceedings denote?
options: The informal hour immediately following Question Hour where members can raise matters without prior notice
The first hour dedicated to questions
questions.explanation: Zero Hour is an Indian parliamentary innovation starting around 12 noon immediately after Question Hour, allowing members to raise urgent public matters.

questions.question: Who decides whether a Bill is a 'Money Bill' or not under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Article 110(3) states that if any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Speaker of the House of the People thereon shall be final.

questions.question: Can a Money Bill be introduced in the Rajya Sabha?
options: No, it can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President
questions.explanation: Under Article 109, a Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). It can only be introduced in Lok Sabha upon presidential recommendation.

questions.question: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha with or without its recommendations?
questions.explanation: Under Article 109(5), if a Money Bill is not returned by the Rajya Sabha to the Lok Sabha within 14 days, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses.

questions.question: What is the status of the 'Anti-Defection Law' under the Indian Constitution, and which schedule contains it?
options: Tenth Schedule (added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985)
questions.explanation: The Anti-Defection Law was inserted into the Tenth Schedule by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985, to disqualify legislators on grounds of defection.

questions.question: Who is the deciding authority on questions of disqualification of members under the Tenth Schedule?
options: The Speaker or Chairman of the respective House
questions.explanation: Paragraph 6 of the Tenth Schedule provides that all questions regarding disqualification on grounds of defection shall be decided by the Chairman or Speaker of the House.

questions.question: Which landmark Supreme Court judgment established that the Speaker's decisions under the Tenth Schedule are subject to judicial review?
questions.explanation: In Kihoto Hollohan (1992), the Supreme Court held that the Speaker functions as a tribunal while deciding Tenth Schedule disqualifications, making decisions subject to judicial review.

questions.question: On July 1, 2026, three historic new criminal justice laws came into force across India. Which Act replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860?
questions.explanation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 replaced the colonial-era Indian Penal Code of 1860, introducing modern definitions, community service punishments, and updated provisions.

questions.question: Which new law replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973 starting July 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 replaced the CrPC 1973, codifying forensic mandates, Zero FIR, timeline-based trials, and electronic summons.

questions.question: Which new law replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 starting July 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 replaced the Indian Evidence Act 1872, recognizing electronic and digital records as primary evidence.

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), what novel non-custodial punishment was introduced for petty offences for the first time in Indian statutory criminal law?
questions.explanation: Community Service was formally introduced as an alternative punishment under Section 4 and specific petty offence sections of the BNS to promote restorative justice.

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), within what time frame must judgment be pronounced following the conclusion of arguments in a trial?
options: Within 30 days (extendable up to 45 days with recorded reasons)
questions.explanation: Section 258/353 of the BNSS mandates that judges pronounce judgment within 30 days from the conclusion of arguments, extendable to a maximum of 45 days for recorded reasons.

questions.question: What does 'Zero FIR' codified under Section 173 of the BNSS entitle a citizen to do?
options: Register an FIR at any police station regardless of jurisdictional boundaries
questions.explanation: Section 173 of the BNSS legally enshrines 'Zero FIR', allowing an individual to lodge an FIR at any police station irrespective of where the crime occurred.

questions.question: For offences punishable with imprisonment of how many years is forensic investigation made mandatory at crime scenes under BNSS?
options: Offences punishable with 7 years or more
questions.explanation: Section 176(3) of the BNSS makes forensic investigation mandatory at the crime scene for all offences punishable with imprisonment of seven years or more.

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the archaic offence of 'Sedition' (Section 124A IPC) was replaced with provisions penalizing what specific act under Section 152?
options: Acts endangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India
questions.explanation: Section 152 of the BNS punishes acts that purposely incite secession, armed rebellion, or subversive activities endangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.

questions.question: What is the maximum period of police custody permitted under Section 187 of the BNSS during the overall 60-day or 90-day investigation period?
options: Up to 15 days, which may be taken in parts across the first 40 or 60 days
15 days strictly continuous within first 15 days only
questions.explanation: Section 187 of the BNSS permits the 15-day police custody to be availed in whole or in parts during the initial 40 or 60 days of the detention period.

questions.question: Which app was launched by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) to help citizens and police officers navigate the transition between IPC and BNS sections?
questions.explanation: NCRB developed the 'Sankalan of Criminal Major Acts' mobile application to compare and cross-reference corresponding sections between old and new laws.

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), how are electronic and digital records treated in terms of evidential value?
options: Given the same legal status and effect as primary evidence in documentary evidence
Admissible only in cyber crime cases
questions.explanation: Section 61 of the BSA establishes that an electronic or digital record shall have the same legal status, effect, and validity as any original paper document.

questions.question: The Union Budget 2026-27 / July economic review announced an internship scheme aiming to provide internship opportunities in 500 top companies to how many youth over 5 years?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme in Top Companies targets providing 12-month internships with a ₹5,000 monthly allowance to 1 crore youth over 5 years.

questions.question: Under the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme launched by the Central Government, Scheme A provides what incentive for first-time employees registered in EPFO?
options: One month's wage up to ₹15,000 in three installments
questions.explanation: Scheme A of the ELI package offers direct benefit transfer of one month's salary (up to ₹15,000) in three installments to first-time formal employees.

questions.question: What special financial package was announced in the Union Budget for Andhra Pradesh's capital development?
options: ₹15,000 crore special financial support through multilateral development agencies
questions.explanation: The Union Budget committed to arranging ₹15,000 crore special financial support for the development of Amaravati as the state capital of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: What is the total outlay announced for the 'Purvodaya' comprehensive development initiative covering Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh?
options: Targeted infrastructure and industrial corridor development package
questions.explanation: The Purvodaya initiative focuses on developing the eastern region of India into an engine of growth through highway corridors, power projects, and temple tourism.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?
questions.explanation: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act 2016 inserted Article 246A, Article 269A, and Article 279A to implement the nationwide Goods and Services Tax.

questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council as per Article 279A of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Under Article 279A, the Union Finance Minister serves as the Chairperson of the GST Council, comprising State Finance Ministers as members.

questions.question: What is the voting weightage distribution in the GST Council between the Central Government and the State Governments?
options: Central Government has one-third weightage, all State Governments combined have two-thirds weightage
questions.explanation: Article 279A(9) stipulates that the Central Government has a one-third weightage of total votes cast, while all State Governments combined have two-thirds weightage, with a 75% majority needed for decisions.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to impose restrictions on trade, commerce, and intercourse between States in the public interest?
questions.explanation: While Article 301 guarantees freedom of trade and commerce throughout India, Article 302 permits Parliament to enact restrictions in the public interest.

questions.question: Right to Property ceased to be a Fundamental Right and became a Constitutional Legal Right under Article 300A via which Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 deleted the Right to Property from Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31, inserting it as a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.

questions.question: Which High Court celebrated the completion of 160+ years since its establishment as one of the three chartered High Courts in 1862?
options: Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras High Courts
questions.explanation: Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras High Courts were established by Letters Patent issued by Queen Victoria under the High Courts Act of 1861, commencing in 1862.

questions.question: Under Article 217 of the Constitution, a High Court Judge holds office until attaining what age?
questions.explanation: High Court judges hold office until 62 years of age (raised from 60 by the 15th Amendment Act 1963), whereas Supreme Court judges retire at 65 years under Article 124.

questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to a newly appointed Judge of a High Court as per Article 219?
options: The Governor of the State (or a person appointed by him)
The Chief Minister of the State
questions.explanation: Article 219 mandates that every person appointed to be a Judge of a High Court shall, before entering upon office, take an oath before the Governor of the State.

questions.question: What is the retirement age of a Judge of the Supreme Court of India under Article 124(2)?
questions.explanation: Under Article 124(2) of the Indian Constitution, a judge of the Supreme Court holds office until attaining the age of sixty-five years.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution confers power on the Supreme Court to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it?
questions.explanation: Article 137 provides that subject to any law made by Parliament or rules under Article 145, the Supreme Court has power to review any judgment pronounced by it.

questions.question: On August 15, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort for which consecutive year?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hoisted the national flag and addressed the country for the 11th consecutive time on Independence Day, surpassing Indira Gandhi's continuous record of 10 speeches.

questions.question: What was the nationwide campaign theme celebrated ahead of Independence Day from August 9 to 15, 2026?
questions.explanation: The third edition of the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign was observed nationwide, encouraging citizens to hoist the National Flag at their homes and click 'Tiranga Selfies'.

questions.question: The Flag Code of India was comprehensively amended in December 2021 to allow the National Flag to be made of which materials?
options: Hand spun, hand woven or machine made cotton, polyester, wool, silk, or khadi bunting
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1.2 of the Flag Code was amended to permit polyester or machine-made flags alongside traditional hand-spun khadi, cotton, and silk.

questions.question: Under the amended Flag Code of India 2002, can the National Flag be flown by the public day and night?
options: Yes, where the Flag is displayed in open or on the house of a member of the public, it may be flown day and night
No, strictly sunrise to sunset only
questions.explanation: The 2022 amendment allows the National Flag to remain hoisted overnight at open private residences provided it is properly displayed.

questions.question: What is the official ratio of width to length of the National Flag of India specified in the Flag Code?
questions.explanation: The ratio of the width (height) to the length of the National Flag of India is strictly 2:3.

questions.question: How many spokes are there in the Ashoka Chakra situated at the centre of the white band of the Indian National Flag?
questions.explanation: The Ashoka Chakra has 24 evenly spaced spokes in navy blue colour, representing the 24 hours of the day and 24 virtues.

questions.question: Who designed the modern National Flag of India which was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on July 22, 1947?
questions.explanation: Freedom fighter and agriculturist Pingali Venkayya designed the swaraj flag that was subsequently modified and adopted by the Constituent Assembly.

questions.question: On which date was the National Anthem of India ('Jana Gana Mana') adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted Rabindranath Tagore's composition 'Jana Gana Mana' as the National Anthem of India on January 24, 1950.

questions.question: What is the formal playing time of the full version of the National Anthem of India?
questions.explanation: The official playing time of the full orchestral version of the Indian National Anthem is approximately 52 seconds (with a short version of 20 seconds).

questions.question: What milestone anniversary did the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) complete on August 28, 2026?
questions.explanation: Launched on August 28, 2014, PMJDY completed 12 years of national financial inclusion, with total bank accounts surpassing 53 crore and deposits exceeding ₹2.3 lakh crore.

questions.question: What is the overdraft (OD) facility limit permitted under PMJDY accounts for eligible account holders?
questions.explanation: The overdraft limit under PMJDY was doubled from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 without collateral conditions for active accounts.

questions.question: Which flagship scheme marked the expansion of free health cover of ₹5 lakh to all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of income?
options: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved universal health coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year to all senior citizens aged 70 years and above under AB-PMJAY.

questions.question: What is the annual health insurance coverage provided per family under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY?
options: ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalization
questions.explanation: AB-PMJAY provides a defined benefit cover of ₹5,00,000 per family per year on a family floater basis across empanelled hospitals.

questions.question: Which organization is the apex statutory body responsible for implementing Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY nationwide?
questions.explanation: The National Health Authority (NHA) is the autonomous attached office of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare responsible for PM-JAY and ABDM.

questions.question: Under the National Quantum Mission (NQM), what is the total approved financial outlay for 2023-2031?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved the National Quantum Mission with an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore to develop quantum computers, communication, and sensors.

questions.question: Which constitutional body is tasked under Article 148 to audit all receipts and expenditures of the Government of India and the state governments?
options: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
questions.explanation: Article 148 establishes the Comptroller and Auditor General of India as the supreme audit institution of the country.

questions.question: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was established in 1964 based on the recommendations of which Committee?
options: K. Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption
questions.explanation: The CVC was set up following the recommendations of the Committee on Prevention of Corruption chaired by Shri K. Santhanam in 1964.

questions.question: Under the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003, what is the term of office for the Central Vigilance Commissioner?
options: 4 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
questions.explanation: The Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners hold office for a term of 4 years from the date of entering office or until age 65.

questions.question: Who is the Chairman of the selection committee that recommends appointments to the Lokpal of India?
questions.explanation: Under Section 4 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013, the Selection Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes the Speaker of Lok Sabha, Leader of Opposition, CJI (or nominee), and an eminent jurist.

questions.question: Who is the current Chairperson of the Lokpal of India appointed in 2024?
questions.explanation: Former Supreme Court judge Justice A.M. Khanwilkar was appointed as the Chairperson of the Lokpal of India.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution can Parliament create a new All India Service if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting?
questions.explanation: Article 312 vests exclusive power in the Rajya Sabha to initiate the creation of one or more All India Services (such as Indian Forest Service, Indian Judicial Service) by a two-thirds majority resolution.

questions.question: How many All India Services currently exist in India under the All India Services Act, 1951?
options: 3 services (IAS, IPS, and IFS - Indian Forest Service)
questions.explanation: There are three All India Services common to the Union and the States: Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and Indian Forest Service (IFS, created in 1966).

questions.question: Which constitutional doctrine ensures that the Legislature cannot bypass constitutional limitations by doing indirectly what it cannot do directly?
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Colourable Legislation is based on the maxim 'What cannot be done directly, cannot also be done indirectly', testing legislative competence.

questions.question: Which constitutional doctrine resolves overlapping legislative jurisdiction between the Union List and State List by examining the true nature and character of the law?
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Pith and Substance determines whether a law substantially falls within the enacting legislature's competence, notwithstanding incidental encroachment on another list.

questions.question: What does Article 254 of the Constitution govern in the context of the Seventh Schedule?
options: Repugnancy or inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and laws made by State Legislatures on Concurrent List subjects
questions.explanation: Article 254 establishes that in case of repugnancy between a Parliamentary enactment and a State law on a Concurrent List subject, the Parliamentary law prevails unless the State law received Presidential assent.

questions.question: What was the projected fiscal deficit target as a percentage of GDP for FY 2024-25 / FY 2025-26 in the Union Budget?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget pegged the fiscal deficit at 4.9% of GDP for FY25, reaffirming the commitment to reach below 4.5% by FY26.

questions.question: What is the capital expenditure (Capex) allocation announced in the Union Budget to boost infrastructure growth?
questions.explanation: The Central Government maintained a record effective capital expenditure outlay of ₹11.11 lakh crore (representing 3.4% of GDP) for infrastructure creation.

questions.question: Under the revised New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC), what was the Standard Deduction for salaried employees increased to?
questions.explanation: The standard deduction for salaried individuals under the new tax regime was enhanced from ₹50,000 to ₹75,000 in the Finance Bill.

questions.question: Under the revised New Tax Regime, income up to what limit is taxed at NIL rate?
questions.explanation: Under the revised tax slabs: 0 to ₹3 lakh is Nil; ₹3-7 lakh is 5%; ₹7-10 lakh is 10%; ₹10-12 lakh is 15%; ₹12-15 lakh is 20%; and above ₹15 lakh is 30%.

questions.question: What is the current policy Repo Rate maintained by the RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in its bi-monthly review?
questions.explanation: The RBI Monetary Policy Committee maintained the benchmark policy repo rate unchanged at 6.50% to align retail inflation with the 4% target.

questions.question: What is the mandated retail inflation target band for the Reserve Bank of India under the flexible inflation targeting framework?
options: 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%)
questions.explanation: Under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act 1934, the inflation target is 4% Consumer Price Index (CPI) with an upper tolerance level of 6% and lower tolerance of 2%.

questions.question: How many members comprise the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of India?
options: 6 members (3 from RBI, 3 external experts appointed by Centre)
questions.explanation: The MPC consists of 6 members: the RBI Governor (Chairperson), Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer, and three external experts nominated by the Central Government.

questions.question: In case of an equality of votes in the RBI Monetary Policy Committee meeting, who has the casting vote?
options: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation: Under Section 45ZL of the RBI Act, each member of the MPC has one vote, and in the event of an equality of votes, the RBI Governor has a second or casting vote.

questions.question: What was India's real GDP growth rate projection for FY25 in the Economic Survey presented in Parliament?
questions.explanation: The Economic Survey conservatively projected India's real GDP growth at 6.5–7.0% for FY 2024-25, highlighting macroeconomic stability.

questions.question: Who presents the Economic Survey in Parliament ahead of the Union Budget?
questions.explanation: While the Economic Survey is authored by the Chief Economic Advisor and his team in the Department of Economic Affairs, it is formally tabled in Parliament by the Union Finance Minister.

questions.question: Who is the current Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) to the Government of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran assumed office as the Chief Economic Advisor to the Government of India in January 2022.

questions.question: Which tax was completely abolished in the Union Budget to encourage startup funding and angel investments in India?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget completely abolished the 'Angel Tax' on all classes of investors to foster the startup ecosystem and boost entrepreneurial investments.

questions.question: The customs duty on gold and silver bars was reduced from 15% to what percentage in the Union Budget?
questions.explanation: Basic customs duty on gold and silver was reduced sharply from 15% to 6% to curb smuggling and stimulate domestic jewellery manufacturing.

questions.question: What is the revised loan ceiling for micro-enterprises under the 'Tarun Plus' category of Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)?
questions.explanation: The budget enhanced the Mudra loan limit under Tarun category from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh for entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid previous loans.

questions.question: Which scheme was announced for providing financial support for loans up to ₹10 lakh for higher education in domestic institutions?
options: Model Skill Loan Scheme / PM Vidya Lakshmi
questions.explanation: The government announced e-vouchers with 3% annual interest subvention for education loans up to ₹10 lakh for youth in domestic higher educational institutions.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the 'Standing Deposit Facility' (SDF) introduced by the RBI in 2022?
options: To absorb surplus liquidity from the commercial banking system without providing collateral
To inject emergency cash to NBFCs
questions.explanation: SDF serves as the floor of the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor, enabling the RBI to absorb uncollateralized overnight liquidity from banks.

questions.question: What is the current Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate relative to the Repo Rate?
options: 25 basis points (0.25%) above the repo rate
questions.explanation: The MSF rate and Bank Rate are positioned 25 basis points above the policy repo rate, forming the upper bound of the policy corridor.

questions.question: Which public sector bank is the largest commercial bank in India by assets, deposits, and branches?
questions.explanation: State Bank of India is a Fortune 500 company and the largest public sector bank in India, holding over a quarter of the market share.

questions.question: Under Basel III regulatory norms, what is the minimum Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) mandated by RBI for Indian commercial banks?
questions.explanation: RBI prescribes a minimum total CRAR of 9% for scheduled commercial banks, which rises to 11.50% including the 2.5% Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB).

questions.question: What is the name of the sovereign entity that manages the government's debt and market borrowings in India?
questions.explanation: Under the RBI Act 1934, the Reserve Bank of India acts as the banker and debt manager to the Central and State Governments.

questions.question: What are 'Treasury Bills' (T-Bills) issued by the Government of India, and what are their standard maturities?
options: Zero-coupon money market instruments with tenors of 91, 182, and 364 days
questions.explanation: Treasury Bills are short-term promissory notes issued at a discount and redeemed at face value by the Central Government in 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day tenors.

questions.question: What is the minimum denomination in which Treasury Bills are auctioned in India?
questions.explanation: Treasury bills are available for a minimum amount of ₹25,000 and in multiples of ₹25,000 thereafter.

questions.question: Which index measures wholesale price fluctuations and is published by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce & Industry?
questions.explanation: WPI tracks headline inflation at the wholesale producer stage, with 2011-12 as its base year.

questions.question: What is the base year for the calculation of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) Combined in India?
questions.explanation: The National Statistical Office (NSO) compiles CPI (Rural, Urban, Combined) using 2012 as the base year.

questions.question: Which weightage category constitutes the largest share in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) basket in India?
questions.explanation: Food and Beverages carry the highest weight of 45.86% in the CPI Combined basket, making food prices a critical driver of headline retail inflation.

questions.question: What milestone record was set by Gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections in March/April 2026?
options: Crossed ₹2.10 lakh crore in a single month
questions.explanation: Gross GST collections hit an all-time high of over ₹2.10 lakh crore, driven by strong domestic transactions and economic compliance.

questions.question: Which state recorded the highest GST collection among all Indian states and Union Territories?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra consistently contributes the largest share of national GST revenue, contributing over ₹30,000 crore monthly.

questions.question: What new settlement mechanism did SEBI launch on an optional basis for 25 scrips in March 2026?
options: Beta version of T+0 rolling settlement cycle
questions.explanation: SEBI rolled out the beta version of optional T+0 settlement for select liquid stocks, settling trades on the same day alongside the existing T+1 cycle.

questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)?
questions.explanation: Madhabi Puri Buch became the first woman and the first private sector professional to lead the market regulator SEBI.

questions.question: India's Foreign Exchange Reserves breached what historic psychological milestone in March 2026?
questions.explanation: India's forex reserves crossed the $650 billion mark, comprising foreign currency assets, gold reserves, SDRs, and reserve tranche in the IMF.

questions.question: Which component forms the largest portion of India's Foreign Exchange Reserves?
questions.explanation: Foreign Currency Assets (FCAs) expressed in US dollars make up over 85% of India's total foreign exchange reserves.

questions.question: Special Drawing Rights (SDR) is an international reserve asset created in 1969 by which multilateral institution?
questions.explanation: The IMF created SDRs to supplement member countries' official reserves, based on a basket of 5 currencies (USD, Euro, Yuan, Yen, Pound Sterling).

questions.question: What is the weightiest currency in the IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR) valuation basket?
questions.explanation: The US Dollar carries the largest weight of approximately 43.38% in the SDR basket, followed by the Euro (29.31%).

questions.question: Which Indian regulatory body issues licenses to 'Payments Banks' and 'Small Finance Banks'?
questions.explanation: Under Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the RBI is the sole licensing authority for differentiated and commercial banks.

questions.question: What is the maximum balance that a customer can hold at the end of the day in a Payments Bank account?
questions.explanation: RBI enhanced the maximum end-of-day deposit limit per individual customer in Payments Banks from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh.

questions.question: Can Payments Banks issue credit cards or undertake lending activities under RBI guidelines?
options: No, they cannot lend or issue credit cards; they can only issue debit cards and accept demand deposits
questions.explanation: Payments Banks are strictly prohibited from lending money or issuing credit cards; their scope is restricted to acceptance of demand deposits and remittance services.

questions.question: What is the minimum percentage of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) that Small Finance Banks must lend to Priority Sectors?
questions.explanation: Small Finance Banks (SFBs) are mandated to allocate at least 75% of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit to the priority sector, compared to 40% for universal banks.

questions.question: What is the Priority Sector Lending (PSL) target for domestic scheduled commercial banks (excluding RRBs & SFBs)?
questions.explanation: Universal commercial banks must direct 40% of their ANBC or credit equivalent of off-balance sheet exposure to priority sectors (agriculture, MSME, housing, etc.).

questions.question: Which institution is the apex regulatory body for housing finance companies in India, supervised by RBI?
questions.explanation: NHB is an all-India financial institution under the Department of Financial Services, operating as the apex developmental institution for the housing sector.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) situated?
questions.explanation: SIDBI, established under an Act of Parliament in 1990 as the principal financial institution for MSMEs, is headquartered in Lucknow.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) located?
questions.explanation: NABARD was established on July 12, 1982, on the recommendations of the B. Sivaraman Committee and has its headquarters in Mumbai.

questions.question: The 'B. Sivaraman Committee' was instrumental in the establishment of which apex institution?
questions.explanation: The Committee to Review Arrangements for Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development (CRAFICARD) chaired by B. Sivaraman recommended creating NABARD.

questions.question: Which organization publishes the 'Financial Stability Report' (FSR) twice every year in India?
questions.explanation: The RBI publishes the biannual Financial Stability Report reflecting the collective assessment of the Sub-Committee of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC).

questions.question: What does 'NPA' stand for in commercial banking, and after how many days of overdue interest/principal is a loan classified as NPA?
questions.explanation: An asset, including a lease asset, becomes non-performing when it ceases to generate income for the bank; a loan is classified as an NPA if interest or installment remains overdue for more than 90 days.

questions.question: What are the three classifications of Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) prescribed by the RBI based on overdue duration?
options: Sub-standard Assets, Doubtful Assets, and Loss Assets
Class A, Class B, and Class C assets
questions.explanation: Banks classify NPAs into: Sub-standard (NPA for <= 12 months), Doubtful (exceeded 12 months in sub-standard), and Loss Asset (identified as uncollectible).

questions.question: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) 2016, what is the default time limit for completing the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP)?
options: 180 days (extendable by 90 days, with overall cap of 330 days)
questions.explanation: Section 12 of the IBC mandates that the CIRP shall be completed within 180 days, extendable by 90 days, with a mandatory outside limit of 330 days including litigation.

questions.question: Which quasi-judicial body adjudicates corporate insolvency matters for companies and LLPs under the IBC?
questions.explanation: The NCLT is the designated Adjudicating Authority for insolvency resolution and liquidation of corporate persons under Part II of the IBC 2016.

questions.question: Which body adjudicates insolvency matters for individuals and partnership firms under Part III of the IBC?
questions.explanation: The Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) is the adjudicating authority for insolvency and bankruptcy proceedings of individuals and partnership firms.

questions.question: What is the legal name of the bad bank set up by the Government and banks to acquire stressed assets from commercial banks?
questions.explanation: NARCL (often termed the 'Bad Bank') was incorporated to consolidate and resolve stressed bank loans above ₹500 crore.

questions.question: What is the function of the India Debt Resolution Company Limited (IDRCL) in coordination with NARCL?
options: Asset management and turnaround company to manage and liquidate assets acquired by NARCL
questions.explanation: While NARCL acquires the non-performing debt, IDRCL acts as the operational turnaround agency to manage, restructure, and maximize asset value.

questions.question: What growth rate did the IMF forecast for India's GDP in its World Economic Outlook released in April 2026?
questions.explanation: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) raised India's GDP growth forecast to 6.8% for FY25, noting robust domestic investment and resilient consumption.

questions.question: What was the headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) retail inflation rate reported for March/April 2026?
questions.explanation: India's retail inflation moderated to 4.85%, staying comfortably within the RBI's target tolerance band of 2% to 6%.

questions.question: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processed how many billion transactions in a single month as reported by NPCI?
questions.explanation: NPCI reported that UPI crossed 13.4 billion monthly transactions with total transaction value exceeding ₹19.78 lakh crore.

questions.question: Who is the umbrella organization for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India?
questions.explanation: NPCI is an initiative of RBI and IBA under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, operating systems like UPI, IMPS, RuPay, and NETC FASTag.

questions.question: In which year was the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) incorporated?
questions.explanation: NPCI was established in 2008 as a 'Not for Profit' Company under Section 25 of the Companies Act 1956 (now Section 8 of Companies Act 2013).

questions.question: Which country became the first European nation to adopt India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) for retail payments?
questions.explanation: France became the first European country to enable UPI payments, allowing Indian tourists to buy tickets for the Eiffel Tower using UPI.

questions.question: Between India and Singapore, which systems were linked for real-time cross-border remittances?
questions.explanation: The linkage between India's UPI and Singapore's PayNow enables instant, low-cost cross-border fund transfers between mobile numbers.

questions.question: Which cross-border payment platform links India's UPI with the UAE's instant payment platform?
questions.explanation: India and UAE integrated UPI with the UAE's instant payment platform 'AANI' and domestic debit card 'Jaywan' based on RuPay technology.

questions.question: What does 'CBDC' stand for in the context of the Reserve Bank of India's digital currency initiative?
options: Central Bank Digital Currency (Digital Rupee / e₹)
questions.explanation: CBDC is the legal tender issued by the Reserve Bank of India in digital form (e₹-Retail and e₹-Wholesale), appearing as a liability on the RBI balance sheet.

questions.question: Under which Section of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, was the legal definition of 'bank note' amended to include digital currency?
options: Section 22 and Section 26 of the RBI Act
questions.explanation: The Finance Act 2022 amended the RBI Act to explicitly encompass digital form currency within the statutory framework of legal tender.

questions.question: What is the difference between CBDC (Digital Rupee) and private cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin?
options: CBDC is sovereign legal tender backed by the central bank; cryptocurrencies are decentralized assets with no sovereign backing
Cryptocurrencies are issued by national governments
questions.explanation: Unlike decentralized volatile private cryptocurrencies, CBDC is a sovereign fiat currency carrying zero default risk and backed 1:1 by the central bank.

questions.question: Does the retail Digital Rupee (e₹-R) earn interest when held in a digital wallet?
options: No, it does not earn any interest, just like physical cash
questions.explanation: To prevent disintermediation of commercial bank deposits, retail CBDC does not bear any interest, mirroring physical currency notes.

questions.question: What is the core mandate of the 'Financial Stability and Development Council' (FSDC)?
options: Macroprudential surveillance, financial sector development, and inter-regulatory coordination
questions.explanation: FSDC is an apex non-statutory council chaired by the Union Finance Minister to maintain financial stability and coordinate between RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, and PFRDA.

questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)?
questions.explanation: Former Financial Services Secretary Debasish Panda serves as the Chairperson of the insurance regulator IRDAI headquartered in Hyderabad.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) located?
questions.explanation: IRDAI was constituted under the IRDA Act 1999 and relocated its statutory headquarters from Delhi to Hyderabad in 2001.

questions.question: Who regulates the National Pension System (NPS) and Atal Pension Yojana (APY) in India?
options: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
questions.explanation: PFRDA is the statutory regulatory body established under the PFRDA Act, 2013, to regulate and promote pension schemes in India.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) located?
questions.explanation: PFRDA has its principal headquarters located in New Delhi.

questions.question: What is the age eligibility criteria for subscribing to the 'Atal Pension Yojana' (APY)?
questions.explanation: APY is open to all bank account holders between 18 and 40 years of age, offering a guaranteed minimum pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per month upon reaching age 60.

questions.question: Income taxpayers have been barred from enrolling in the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) starting from which date?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Finance notified that any citizen who is or has been an income taxpayer shall not be eligible to join the Atal Pension Yojana post October 1, 2022.

questions.question: What is the maximum investment limit under the Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS) per individual as revised in 2023?
questions.explanation: The maximum deposit limit for the Senior Citizens Savings Scheme was doubled from ₹15 lakh to ₹30 lakh.

questions.question: What is the investment tenure of the Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) scheme issued by the RBI on behalf of the Government?
questions.explanation: SGBs have a total tenure of 8 years, with early encashment/redemption permitted after the fifth year on interest payment dates.

questions.question: What is the fixed annual interest rate paid to investors on the initial nominal investment value of Sovereign Gold Bonds?
questions.explanation: Investors receive a guaranteed semi-annual interest of 2.50% per annum on the initial issue price, in addition to capital gains on redemption at market gold price.

questions.question: Capital gains tax on redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds by an individual investor at maturity is:
questions.explanation: Under Section 47 of the Income Tax Act, capital gains tax arising on redemption of SGB to an individual is completely exempt.

questions.question: Which agency in India compiles and releases the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
questions.explanation: The NSO under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation compiles IIP monthly with 2011-12 as the base year.

questions.question: What is the weightage of the 'Eight Core Industries' in the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
questions.explanation: The Eight Core Industries (Refinery Products, Electricity, Steel, Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Cement, and Fertilizers) comprise 40.27% of total weight in IIP.

questions.question: Which of the eight core industries carries the highest individual weightage in the Index of Eight Core Industries?
questions.explanation: Petroleum Refinery Products has the highest weight of 28.04%, followed by Electricity at 19.85% and Steel at 17.92%.

questions.question: Which core industry carries the lowest weightage in the Index of Eight Core Industries?
questions.explanation: Fertilizers has the smallest weightage of 2.63% among the eight core sectors.

questions.question: What is the FDI limit permitted in the insurance sector in India under the automatic route?
questions.explanation: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in insurance companies is permitted up to 74% under the automatic approval route.

questions.question: What is the FDI limit allowed in defence manufacturing under the automatic route in India?
options: Up to 74% (and up to 100% via government approval route for modern technology)
questions.explanation: FDI in defence sector is permitted up to 74% under the automatic route and above 74% through the government route wherever modern technology is accessed.

questions.question: Which country was the largest source of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) equity inflows into India during FY 2023-24 / 2025?
questions.explanation: Singapore continues to be the largest source country for FDI equity inflows into India, followed by Mauritius and the United States.

questions.question: Which sector attracted the highest share of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) equity inflows in India?
questions.explanation: Computer Software and Hardware attracted the highest volume of foreign equity investments, followed by the financial and business services sector.

questions.question: Which Indian state received the highest share of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra received the largest share of total FDI inflows in India, accounting for over 30% of total national receipts.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the 'Trade Receivables Discounting System' (TReDS) regulated by RBI?
options: Facilitating discounting of trade receivables of MSMEs from corporate and government buyers through multiple financiers
questions.explanation: TReDS is an electronic institutional mechanism that enables MSMEs to auction and discount their trade bills against large corporates, unlocking working capital.

questions.question: Which organization operates the 'GeM' (Government e-Marketplace) portal for public procurement in India?
