options: Special Purpose Vehicle (GeM SPV) under Department of Commerce
questions.explanation: GeM is an end-to-end online marketplace facilitating transparent procurement of common use goods and services required by central and state government ministries and PSUs.

questions.question: What is the mandated annual procurement target from MSEs (Micro and Small Enterprises) for Central Ministries and CPSEs under the Public Procurement Policy?
options: 25% of total annual purchases (including 4% from SC/ST and 3% from Women entrepreneurs)
questions.explanation: CPSEs and Central Ministries are mandated to procure a minimum of 25% of their total annual procurement of goods and services from Micro and Small Enterprises.

questions.question: What does 'PLI' stand for in the context of government industrial schemes?
questions.explanation: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme provides financial incentives on incremental sales of goods manufactured in domestic units across 14 key sectors.

questions.question: How many strategic sectors are covered under the Government of India's flagship Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme?
questions.explanation: The PLI scheme covers 14 champion sectors including Mobile & Electronics, Pharmaceuticals, Automobiles & Auto Components, Telecom, and High-Efficiency Solar PV Modules.

questions.question: Which regulatory authority oversees credit rating agencies operating in India?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates credit rating agencies (such as CRISIL, ICRA, CARE, and India Ratings) under the SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) Regulations, 1999.

questions.question: Which credit rating agency was established in 1987 as the first credit rating agency in India?
options: CRISIL (Credit Rating Information Services of India Limited)
questions.explanation: CRISIL, promoted by ICICI and UTI, was incorporated in 1987 as India's pioneer credit rating institution.

questions.question: What does 'CAMELS' rating framework used by the RBI to assess commercial banks stand for?
options: Capital adequacy, Asset quality, Management, Earnings, Liquidity, and Sensitivity to market risk
Cash, Assets, Margin, Equity, Liability, Solvency
Credit, Audit, Management, Expense, Loans, Security
Capital, Advances, Market, Efficiency, Losses, Stability
questions.explanation: CAMELS is an international supervisory rating system examining Capital adequacy, Asset quality, Management efficiency, Earnings ability, Liquidity position, and Sensitivity to market risk.

questions.question: What is the maximum guarantee cover available under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)?
options: Up to ₹5 crore per borrowing unit
questions.explanation: The Government and SIDBI enhanced the credit guarantee ceiling under CGTMSE to ₹5 crore with reduced annual guarantee fees.

questions.question: Who set up the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)?
questions.explanation: CGTMSE was jointly established by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) and the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) in 2000.

questions.question: Under the revised MSME classification effective July 1, 2020, what is the composite criteria for a 'Micro' enterprise?
questions.explanation: Micro enterprises are defined by Investment in Plant & Machinery <= ₹1 crore and Annual Turnover <= ₹5 crore.

questions.question: What is the composite criteria for a 'Small' enterprise under the official MSME classification?
questions.explanation: Small enterprises are defined by Investment in Plant & Machinery <= ₹10 crore and Annual Turnover <= ₹50 crore.

questions.question: What is the composite criteria for a 'Medium' enterprise under the official MSME definition?
questions.explanation: Medium enterprises are defined by Investment in Plant & Machinery <= ₹50 crore and Annual Turnover <= ₹250 crore.

questions.question: Which portal is the single online registration platform for obtaining an MSME certificate in India?
questions.explanation: Udyam Registration is the sole zero-fee, paperless government portal for formal registration of MSMEs based on self-declaration and Aadhaar/PAN integration.

questions.question: Which organization publishes the Global Economic Prospects report biannually in January and June?
questions.explanation: The World Bank issues the Global Economic Prospects report examining global economic growth dynamics and emerging market debt trends.

questions.question: Which organization releases the 'World Economic Outlook' (WEO) report twice a year?
questions.explanation: The IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook in April and October with growth updates in January and July.

questions.question: Which institution publishes the 'Trade and Development Report'?
options: UNCTAD (United Nations Conference on Trade and Development)
questions.explanation: UNCTAD publishes the annual Trade and Development Report analyzing global trade trends, macroeconomics, and development strategies.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the New Development Bank (NDB / BRICS Bank) located?
questions.explanation: The New Development Bank established by BRICS member states in 2014 is headquartered in Shanghai, China.

questions.question: According to the RBI Financial Stability Report released in June 2026, the Gross Non-Performing Assets (GNPA) ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks fell to what multi-year low?
questions.explanation: The Gross NPA ratio of commercial banks declined to a 12-year low of 2.8% by March 2024/2026, highlighting the robust health of the Indian banking balance sheet.

questions.question: What was the Net Non-Performing Assets (NNPA) ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks recorded in the RBI Financial Stability Report?
questions.explanation: The Net NPA ratio of banks dropped to 0.6%, reflecting strong provisioning coverage and sustained asset quality improvements.

questions.question: What is the Provisioning Coverage Ratio (PCR) maintained by Indian scheduled commercial banks as per RBI data?
questions.explanation: The banking system's Provisioning Coverage Ratio stood healthy at over 76%, safeguarding lenders against potential credit shocks.

questions.question: International credit rating agency S&P Global Ratings revised its sovereign rating outlook for India from 'Stable' to what in mid-2026?
questions.explanation: S&P upgraded India's outlook from Stable to Positive on robust economic growth, sound macroeconomic fundamentals, and narrowing fiscal deficit.

questions.question: What is India's sovereign credit rating assigned by major global rating agencies (Moody's, S&P, Fitch)?
options: Lowest investment grade (Baa3 by Moody's; BBB- by S&P and Fitch)
questions.explanation: India is currently rated at the lowest investment grade—Baa3 by Moody's and BBB- by S&P and Fitch—with an outlook reflecting positive upward trajectory.

questions.question: What does 'G-Sec' stand for in Indian financial markets?
questions.explanation: Government Securities (G-Secs) are tradable sovereign instruments issued by the RBI on behalf of the Government to finance fiscal deficit.

questions.question: Which global bond index formally included Indian Government Bonds (FAR - Fully Accessible Route securities) starting June 2026?
options: J.P. Morgan Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets (GBI-EM)
questions.explanation: J.P. Morgan officially began phased inclusion of Indian G-Secs in its flagship GBI-EM Global Diversified suite, unlocking billions in foreign debt inflows.

questions.question: What is the maximum targeted weightage of Indian Government Bonds in the J.P. Morgan GBI-EM index upon full inclusion?
questions.explanation: Indian bonds are capped at the maximum index weight of 10%, phasing in at 1% weight addition each month over a 10-month period.

questions.question: What is the 'Fully Accessible Route' (FAR) introduced by the RBI in 2020?
options: A channel allowing non-residents to invest in specified government securities without any quantitative limits
A scheme for foreign equity IPOs
questions.explanation: The FAR scheme designates specific government dated securities as eligible for unlimited foreign portfolio investment.

questions.question: What is the 'RBI Retail Direct' scheme launched to encourage individual investors in government debt?
options: A portal allowing retail individual investors to directly open Gilt Securities Accounts (RDG Accounts) with RBI to buy G-Secs, T-Bills, and SGBs
questions.explanation: RBI Retail Direct enables individual retail investors to open free Gilt accounts directly with the Reserve Bank and participate in primary auctions and secondary trading without intermediaries.

questions.question: What is the 'NDS-OM' platform operated by the Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL)?
options: Negotiated Dealing System-Order Matching (electronic trading platform for government securities)
questions.explanation: NDS-OM is the screen-based electronic anonymous order-matching system for trading in government securities in the secondary market.

questions.question: Who acts as the Central Counterparty (CCP) for clearing and settlement of trades in G-Secs, money market instruments, and foreign exchange in India?
questions.explanation: CCIL, set up in 2001, provides guaranteed clearing and settlement for transactions in Government securities, repos, interest rate derivatives, and forex.

questions.question: What is the minimum maturity period for Commercial Paper (CP) issued in the Indian money market?
questions.explanation: Commercial Paper (CP) is an unsecured money market instrument issued as a promissory note with a minimum maturity of 7 days and maximum of up to one year.

questions.question: What is the minimum denomination of Commercial Paper (CP) in India?
questions.explanation: Commercial Paper is issued in denominations of ₹5 lakh and multiples thereof to eligible corporate borrowers and primary dealers.

questions.question: What is a 'Certificate of Deposit' (CD) and who can issue it in India?
options: A negotiable money market instrument issued by Scheduled Commercial Banks and select All-India Financial Institutions
Issued by local co-operative societies only
questions.explanation: Certificates of Deposit are negotiable short-term instruments issued in demat form by commercial banks for funds deposited for a specified time period.

questions.question: What is the minimum maturity period of a Certificate of Deposit (CD) issued by commercial banks in India?
questions.explanation: CDs issued by banks have a minimum tenor of 7 days and a maximum tenor of up to one year.

questions.question: What is 'Call Money' in the Indian inter-bank money market?
options: Borrowing or lending of funds on an overnight (one-day) basis
questions.explanation: Call Money refers to inter-bank funds borrowed or lent for one single day (overnight). Funds for 2 to 14 days are called Notice Money; beyond 14 days is Term Money.

questions.question: What is 'Notice Money' in the money market?
options: Funds borrowed or lent for a period between 2 days and 14 days
questions.explanation: In inter-bank money market parlance, borrowing or lending of funds for a duration spanning 2 to 14 days is termed Notice Money.

questions.question: What is 'Term Money' in the Indian financial market?
options: Funds borrowed or lent for a maturity period exceeding 14 days (up to 1 year)
questions.explanation: Borrowing or lending of market funds for tenors greater than 14 days and up to one year is classified as Term Money.

questions.question: What is a 'Tri-Party Repo' (TREPS) introduced in the Indian money market?
options: A repo contract where a third entity (CCIL) acts as an intermediary between borrower and lender for collateral management and settlement
A loan to three state governments
questions.explanation: TREPS is a facilitated repo transaction where CCIL manages collateral, margins, and settlements between borrowing and lending institutions.

questions.question: Which body fixes the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) and ceiling prices of essential medicines in India?
questions.explanation: NPPA, an attached office of the Department of Pharmaceuticals, fixes and revises prices of controlled drugs and medical devices under the DPCO 2013.

questions.question: What does 'DPCO' stand for in pharmaceutical regulation?
questions.explanation: The Drugs (Prices Control) Order is an order issued by the Central Government under Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, to regulate prices of essential formulations.

questions.question: Under which statutory Act does the Central Government declare commodities as 'Essential Commodities'?
questions.explanation: The Essential Commodities Act, 1955 empowers the government to regulate the production, supply, and distribution of essential goods to prevent hoarding and black-marketing.

questions.question: What is 'Minimum Support Price' (MSP) and who recommends it to the Government of India?
options: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)
questions.explanation: CACP, an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture, recommends MSPs for 22 mandated crops and Fair & Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane.

questions.question: How many mandated crops are covered under the Minimum Support Price (MSP) framework recommended by CACP?
options: 22 mandated crops (plus Fair & Remunerative Price for sugarcane)
questions.explanation: CACP recommends MSPs for 22 mandated agricultural crops (14 Kharif, 6 Rabi, and 2 commercial crops) along with FRP for sugarcane.

questions.question: What was the major change in Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on financial assets announced in the Union Budget?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget rationalized capital gains: Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on financial and non-financial assets was unified at 12.5%.

questions.question: What was the revised Short Term Capital Gains (STCG) tax rate on specified listed financial assets under Section 111A?
questions.explanation: STCG tax on specified equity and equity-oriented mutual fund units was increased from 15% to 20%.

questions.question: What was the enhanced exemption limit for Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares per financial year?
questions.explanation: The annual tax exemption limit for aggregate LTCG from equity shares and equity mutual funds was enhanced from ₹1,00,000 to ₹1,25,000.

questions.question: What change was made to the Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on Futures and Options (F&O) in the Budget?
options: Increased to 0.02% on futures and 0.1% on options premium
questions.explanation: To curb speculative retail trading in equity derivatives, STT on futures was hiked to 0.02% and on options to 0.1%.

questions.question: The corporate tax rate on foreign companies operating in India was reduced from 40% to what percentage in the Budget?
questions.explanation: To attract foreign capital and multinational corporations, the corporate income tax rate on foreign companies was lowered from 40% to 35%.

questions.question: What is the basic customs duty on critical minerals like Lithium, Copper, Nickel, and Cobalt modified to in the Budget?
questions.explanation: The government fully exempted basic customs duty on 25 critical minerals (including lithium, copper, nickel, cobalt, and rare earths) to boost clean energy tech.

questions.question: What financial allocation was dedicated to agriculture and allied sectors in the Union Budget for FY 2024-25 / 2026?
questions.explanation: The Union Finance Minister earmarked ₹1.52 lakh crore for agriculture and allied sectors to drive farmer welfare, natural farming, and digital public infrastructure.

questions.question: Under the 'Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for Agriculture', coverage for how many farmers and their lands was announced for digital crop survey?
options: Digital crop survey for 6 crore farmers across 400 districts
questions.explanation: The Budget announced implementation of DPI in agriculture in partnership with states to conduct digital crop surveys for 6 crore farmers.

questions.question: What is the total allocation provided for the Ministry of Defence in the Union Budget, maintaining its position as the highest allocated ministry?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Defence received the highest allocation of ₹6.22 lakh crore, constituting 13% of the total Union Budget expenditure.

questions.question: What percentage of the defence capital acquisition budget is reserved for procurement from domestic defense industries?
questions.explanation: The Defence Ministry earmarked 75% of its capital modernisation budget for domestic procurement under the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative.

questions.question: What is the allocation announced for the Ministry of Railways in the Union Budget?
questions.explanation: Indian Railways was allocated a record capital outlay of ₹2.52 lakh crore to upgrade passenger safety, build dedicated freight corridors, and deploy Kavach.

questions.question: What is 'Kavach' developed indigenously by Indian Railways?
options: An Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system to prevent train collisions
questions.explanation: Kavach is an indigenously developed SIL-4 certified Automatic Train Protection system designed to avert signal passing at danger and head-on collisions.

questions.question: Which organization developed the indigenous Kavach train protection technology?
options: Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO), Lucknow
questions.explanation: Kavach was designed and tested by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) in collaboration with Indian technology partners.

questions.question: What is the primary aim of the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan?
options: Multi-modal connectivity infrastructure to reduce logistics costs and break departmental silos
questions.explanation: PM GatiShakti brings 16 ministries together on a GIS platform for synchronized planning and execution of multi-modal connectivity projects.

questions.question: What is the target for India's logistics cost as a percentage of GDP under the National Logistics Policy?
options: Reduce from 13-14% to single digits (around 8%) by 2030
questions.explanation: The National Logistics Policy aims to reduce logistics costs to global benchmarks (around 8% of GDP) to enhance trade competitiveness.

questions.question: Which international index published by the World Bank evaluates national logistics performance, where India improved to 38th rank?
questions.explanation: India moved up to 38th position out of 139 nations in the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index (LPI), driven by port modernization and digitalization.

questions.question: Which major container transshipment port in Kerala commenced commercial operations in July 2026?
options: Vizhinjam International Transshipment Deepwater Multipurpose Seaport
questions.explanation: Vizhinjam International Seaport in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, developed by Adani Ports, welcomed its first mother vessels, positioning India as a global bunkering hub.

questions.question: What is the natural draft depth of the Vizhinjam International Seaport, enabling it to berth the world's largest ultra-large container vessels?
questions.explanation: Vizhinjam boasts a natural water depth of up to 20 metres, requiring minimal dredging and allowing 24,000+ TEU mega container vessels to dock directly.

questions.question: Which Indian port was renamed as 'Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port' in 2020?
questions.explanation: Kolkata Port Trust, India's oldest operational riverine port, was rechristened as Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port on its 150th anniversary.

questions.question: Which Indian port was rechristened as 'Deendayal Port'?
questions.explanation: Kandla Port in Kutch, Gujarat, was officially renamed Deendayal Port in honor of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya.

questions.question: Which port was named as 'V.O. Chidambaranar Port'?
questions.explanation: The Major Port of Tuticorin was renamed V.O. Chidambaranar Port in memory of the freedom fighter who pioneered indigenous merchant shipping.

questions.question: How many 'Major Ports' are there in India under the administrative jurisdiction of the Central Government?
options: 12 Major Ports (plus Vadhavan Port approved as the 13th)
questions.explanation: There are 12 operational Major Ports in India, with the Union Cabinet giving approval for the 13th major greenfield port at Vadhavan in Maharashtra.

questions.question: Where is the newly approved ₹76,220 crore greenfield mega port project 'Vadhavan Port' located?
questions.explanation: The all-weather Vadhavan deep-water port is located in Palghar district, Maharashtra, designed to rank among the top 10 container ports globally.

questions.question: What is the equity shareholding structure in the Vadhavan Port Project SPV?
options: JNPA holds 74% and Maharashtra Maritime Board (MMB) holds 26%
questions.explanation: The project is developed by Vadhavan Port Project Limited (VPPL), an SPV formed by Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (74%) and Maharashtra Maritime Board (26%).

questions.question: Which port is the largest container handling port in India, accounting for over 50% of the nation's total containerized cargo?
options: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) / Nhava Sheva
questions.explanation: JNPA (Nhava Sheva) in Navi Mumbai is the premier public container port in India, achieving record throughput of over 6.4 million TEUs.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India in its August 2026 Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) review projected India's real GDP growth for FY 2024-25 / 2026-27 at what rate?
questions.explanation: The RBI projected real GDP growth at 7.2% with balanced risks, driven by rural demand recovery and high manufacturing capacity utilization.

questions.question: What retail CPI inflation projection did the RBI maintain for the full fiscal year in August 2026?
questions.explanation: The RBI estimated retail headline CPI inflation at 4.5% for the year, anticipating favourable monsoon impact on food prices.

questions.question: What is the total Assets Under Management (AUM) crossed by the National Pension System (NPS) and Atal Pension Yojana as of August 2026?
questions.explanation: PFRDA announced that aggregate pension assets under management under NPS and APY crossed ₹12.5 lakh crore, reflecting rapid growth in non-government corporate subscribers.

questions.question: What is the minimum pension guaranteed under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2026 for central government employees?
options: ₹10,000 per month for employees with minimum 10 years of service
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) ensuring an assured minimum pension of ₹10,000 per month for central employees with at least 10 years of service.

questions.question: Under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), what percentage of average basic pay drawn over the last 12 months is guaranteed as an assured pension?
options: 50% of average basic pay for minimum 25 years of qualifying service
questions.explanation: Under UPS, employees with at least 25 years of service receive an assured pension of 50% of the average basic pay drawn in the last 12 months prior to superannuation.

questions.question: Under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), what is the increased contribution rate of the Central Government towards employees' pension?
questions.explanation: The Central Government increased its contribution from 14% to 18.5% of basic pay + DA under the UPS framework, while employee contribution remains unchanged at 10%.

questions.question: From which date will the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) take effect for Central Government employees?
questions.explanation: The Unified Pension Scheme takes effect from April 1, offering employees the choice to opt between NPS and the new assured UPS.

questions.question: Who chaired the committee constituted by the Finance Ministry to review the pension system that led to the formulation of UPS?
questions.explanation: The committee was chaired by Dr. T.V. Somanathan (then Finance Secretary, later appointed Cabinet Secretary of India).

questions.question: What is the family pension percentage assured to the spouse of a deceased employee under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS)?
options: 60% of the pension of the employee immediately before his or her demise
questions.explanation: Under UPS, an assured family pension at the rate of 60% of the employee's pension is provided to the spouse upon the pensioner's demise.

questions.question: What indexation benefit is provided to pensioners under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS)?
options: Dearness Relief indexation based on All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW)
questions.explanation: Pensions under UPS feature Dearness Relief indexation linked to AICPI-IW, mirroring the inflation-protection of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS).

questions.question: Which organization releases the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW)?
options: Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour and Employment
questions.explanation: The Labour Bureau, an attached office of the Ministry of Labour & Employment, compiles and releases CPI-IW with base year 2016 = 100.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Labour Bureau located?
questions.explanation: The Labour Bureau functions with operational headquarters at Chandigarh and Shimla, responsible for industrial wages and consumer price index series.

questions.question: What is the base year currently used for the Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL)?
questions.explanation: CPI for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL) and Rural Labourers (CPI-RL) are compiled by the Labour Bureau with base year 1986-87 = 100.

questions.question: What is the minimum wages revision mechanism used by the Central Government under the Code on Wages, 2019?
questions.explanation: The Code on Wages empowers the Central Government to determine a statutory National Floor Minimum Wage, below which no State Government can set minimum wages.

questions.question: How many central labour laws were consolidated and subsumed into the Four Labour Codes?
questions.explanation: The Government of India simplified 29 existing central labour enactments into four streamlined codes: Wages, Social Security, Industrial Relations, and OSH.

questions.question: What are the names of the Four Labour Codes enacted by Parliament?
options: Code on Wages; Industrial Relations Code; Social Security Code; Occupational Safety, Health & Working Conditions Code
Employment Code, Factory Code, Wage Code, Pension Code
questions.explanation: The Four Labour Codes are: Code on Wages (2019), Industrial Relations Code (2020), Code on Social Security (2020), and OSH&WC Code (2020).

questions.question: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, what novel category of non-traditional workers was granted statutory social security recognition for the first time?
questions.explanation: The Code on Social Security legally recognized gig workers and platform workers, mandating a Social Security Fund financed by platform aggregators (1-2% of turnover).

questions.question: Which state in India enacted the pioneering 'Platform Based Gig Workers (Registration and Welfare) Act' in 2023?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan became the first state in India to pass dedicated legislation setting up a Welfare Board and social security cess for platform gig workers.

questions.question: Which state announced a ₹5 lakh accidental and life insurance scheme for gig workers in 2023-24 / 2026?
questions.explanation: Southern states including Karnataka and Telangana rolled out dedicated social security insurance covers for registered gig and delivery personnel.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the 'e-Shram' portal developed by the Ministry of Labour and Employment?
options: Creating a comprehensive national database of unorganized workers seeded with Aadhaar
questions.explanation: The e-Shram portal registers unorganized workers across informal sectors, issuing a 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) for delivery of welfare schemes.

questions.question: How many unorganized workers have registered on the e-Shram portal as of 2024-2026?
questions.explanation: Over 30 crore informal and unorganized workers have enrolled on e-Shram, enabling seamless portability of social security benefits.

questions.question: What is the monthly contribution amount under the 'Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan' (PM-SYM) pension scheme for eligible unorganized workers?
options: ₹55 to ₹200 per month depending on entry age (matched 50:50 by Central Government)
questions.explanation: PM-SYM requires a monthly voluntary contribution of ₹55 to ₹200 (age 18 to 40), with an equal 50% matching contribution by the Central Government, ensuring a ₹3,000 monthly pension.

questions.question: What is the guaranteed monthly pension provided under the PM-SYM scheme after attaining the age of 60 years?
questions.explanation: PM-SYM guarantees a minimum monthly pension of ₹3,000 to beneficiaries upon attaining the age of 60 years.

questions.question: Which agency serves as the pension fund manager and oversees pension payout for PM-SYM beneficiaries?
questions.explanation: LIC is the designated Pension Fund Manager responsible for pension fund management and direct pension disbursements under PM-SYM.

questions.question: What is the statutory interest rate credited on Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) accumulations for active members?
questions.explanation: The Central Board of Trustees of EPFO recommended and the Finance Ministry ratified an 8.25% annual interest rate for EPF subscribers.

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the names of the four astronaut designates for India's maiden human spaceflight mission 'Gaganyaan' in February 2026 at VSSC, Thiruvananthapuram. Who among the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: The four selected IAF astronaut designates are Group Captain Prashanth Balakrishnan Nair, Group Captain Ajit Krishnan, Group Captain Angad Pratap, and Wing Commander Shubhanshu Shukla. (Rakesh Sharma was India's first cosmonaut in 1984).

questions.question: Which IAF astronaut designate was selected to fly to the International Space Station (ISS) on the Axiom-4 (Ax-4) commercial mission with NASA?
questions.explanation: ISRO and NASA finalized that Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla will serve as the primary mission pilot on the Axiom-4 mission to the ISS, with Prashanth Nair as backup.

questions.question: What was the official focal theme of National Science Day celebrated across India on February 28, 2026?
options: Future of STI: Impacts on Education
Integrated Approach in Science and Technology
questions.explanation: The theme 'Indigenous Technologies for Viksit Bharat' underscored domestic scientific innovation, Atmanirbharta, and grassroots technological breakthroughs.

questions.question: National Science Day on February 28 commemorates which pathbreaking scientific discovery by Sir C.V. Raman in 1928?
options: The Raman Effect (inelastic scattering of photons)
questions.explanation: National Science Day marks the discovery of the 'Raman Effect' on February 28, 1928, for which Sir C.V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.

questions.question: What is the financial allocation approved by the Union Cabinet for the comprehensive 'IndiaAI Mission' to build domestic compute infrastructure?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved the IndiaAI Mission with a financial outlay of ₹10,372 crore to procure 10,000+ GPUs and establish foundational multi-modal AI models.

questions.question: Which city hosted the mega multilateral naval exercise 'MILAN 2026' featuring navies from over 50 friendly foreign countries?
questions.explanation: Exercise MILAN 2026 was hosted by the Eastern Naval Command in Visakhapatnam ('City of Destiny'), featuring sea-phase drills and an International City Parade.

questions.question: What was the theme of the Multilateral Naval Exercise 'MILAN 2026'?
options: Forging Naval Alliances: Dynamic, Synergy, Cohesion
Security and Growth for All in the Region
questions.explanation: The core theme of MILAN 2026 centered on 'Forging Naval Alliances: Dynamic, Synergy, Cohesion' to promote maritime safety and open sea lines of communication.

questions.question: Which indigenous surface-to-air missile system was successfully demonstrated during Indian Air Force exercises, engaging multiple targets simultaneously?
options: SAMAR (Surface to Air Missile for Assured Retaliation)
questions.explanation: The IAF operationalized SAMAR, an indigenous short-range air defence system developed by IAF base repair depots using refurbished Vympel R-73 missiles.

questions.question: What is the maximum strike range of the DRDO-developed 'Akash-NG' (New Generation) surface-to-air missile system?
questions.explanation: Akash-NG is an advanced air defence missile with an active RF seeker, dual-pulse solid rocket motor, and an interception range of around 70-80 km.

questions.question: Which research institute under the Department of Atomic Energy operates the 'Dhruva' high-flux research reactor at Trombay?
options: Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR)
questions.explanation: BARC in Trombay, Mumbai, operates the 100 MWth Dhruva reactor, which produces medical radioisotopes and supports basic nuclear research.

questions.question: Where is the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) located, specializing in Fast Breeder Reactor technologies?
questions.explanation: IGCAR is located at Kalpakkam, south of Chennai, home to the Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR) and the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR).

questions.question: What nuclear fuel cycle technology does India's Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam utilize as part of Stage II of India's Nuclear Power Programme?
questions.explanation: Stage II utilizes Mixed Oxide (MOX) fuel of Plutonium-239 (from Stage 1 spent fuel) and Uranium-238 to breed more fissile material than it consumes.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the Father of India's Three-Stage Nuclear Power Programme?
questions.explanation: Dr. Homi Bhabha envisioned the 3-stage programme to sequentially utilize India's modest uranium reserves and vast thorium deposits (monazite sands of Kerala).

questions.question: What fuel will be primarily utilized in the third stage of India's nuclear power programme to achieve long-term energy independence?
questions.explanation: Stage 3 focuses on Advanced Heavy Water Reactors (AHWR) using Thorium-232, which absorbs neutrons to transmute into fissile Uranium-233.

questions.question: Which Indian state has the largest known reserves of Thorium in its monazite beach sands?
questions.explanation: Kerala's coastal placer sands, along with deposits in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, contain the world's richest monazite sands yielding thorium.

questions.question: Which propulsion module does the launch vehicle LVM3 (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mk III) use for its cryogenic upper stage?
questions.explanation: ISRO's heavy-lift LVM3 uses the indigenous CE-20 cryogenic engine in its C25 upper stage, powered by liquid oxygen (LOX) and liquid hydrogen (LH2).

questions.question: What is the human-rated version of the LVM3 rocket designated as for the Gaganyaan mission?
questions.explanation: ISRO modified all systems, avionics, and safety margins of LVM3 to create the Human-Rated LVM3 (HLVM3) to carry the orbital module.

questions.question: What is the name of the humanoid robot developed by ISRO to fly on uncrewed Gaganyaan test missions ahead of human astronauts?
questions.explanation: Vyommitra is a female spacefaring humanoid robot designed to monitor capsule environmental parameters, operate switch panels, and simulate crew functions.

questions.question: Where is ISRO's second spaceport for commercial small satellite launches being established?
questions.explanation: The second spaceport is coming up at Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu, offering a direct southward trajectory for SSLV without having to dogleg around Sri Lanka.

questions.question: Why does launching polar satellites from Kulasekarapattinam provide a major operational advantage over Sriharikota?
options: Allows a straight southward flight path over the ocean without requiring an expensive eastward dogleg manoeuvre to avoid Sri Lankan airspace
questions.explanation: Launches from Sriharikota must dogleg eastward to bypass Sri Lanka's landmass, consuming rocket payload fuel; Kulasekarapattinam allows a direct straight trajectory.

questions.question: Which small satellite launch vehicle was developed by ISRO specifically for on-demand low-cost launches of mini-satellites up to 500 kg?
questions.explanation: SSLV is a 3-stage all-solid rocket with a liquid velocity trimming module (VTM), requiring minimal launch infrastructure and a turnaround of days.

questions.question: Who is the current Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Secretary, Department of Space?
questions.explanation: Eminent aerospace engineer S. Somanath serves as the Chairman of ISRO and Secretary of the Department of Space.

questions.question: Who is the current Chairman of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)?
questions.explanation: Distinguished scientist Dr. Samir V. Kamat serves as the Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman of DRDO.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Missile Woman of India' for her leading role as Project Director for the Agni-IV missile?
questions.explanation: Dr. Tessy Thomas is celebrated as India's 'Missile Woman' for directing key Agni series missile development programmes at DRDO.

questions.question: Who was the Project Director of the historic Chandrayaan-3 mission that landed at the lunar south polar region?
questions.explanation: Senior ISRO scientist P. Veeramuthuvel served as the Project Director of the triumphant Chandrayaan-3 mission.

questions.question: In March 2026, DRDO successfully conducted the first flight test of the indigenous Agni-5 missile equipped with MIRV technology under which mission name?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the success of 'Mission Divyastra'—the maiden flight test of the Agni-5 intercontinental ballistic missile with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) technology.

questions.question: What does 'MIRV' stand for in strategic missile technology?
questions.explanation: MIRV technology allows a single ballistic missile to deliver multiple nuclear warheads directed at distinct, widely separated targets hundreds of kilometres apart.

questions.question: With the success of Mission Divyastra, India joined an elite club of which nations possessing operational MIRV missile capability?
options: USA, Russia, China, UK, France, and India
Five permanent UNSC members and North Korea
questions.explanation: Only the US, Russia, the UK, France, and China previously possessed tested operational MIRV technology.

questions.question: What is the estimated strike range of India's indigenous Agni-5 intercontinental ballistic missile?
questions.explanation: Agni-5 is a three-stage solid-fueled road-mobile ICBM with an operational range exceeding 5,000 km, bringing all of Asia and parts of Europe within strike reach.

questions.question: From which location off the coast of Odisha did DRDO conduct the historic Mission Divyastra test flight?
options: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island (Wheeler Island)
questions.explanation: The test was conducted from the Integrated Test Range at Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the coast of Bhadrak, Odisha.

questions.question: Which joint military exercise was conducted between the Indian Army and the Uzbekistan Armed Forces in March-April 2026?
questions.explanation: Exercise DUSTLIK is the annual bilateral military drill between India and Uzbekistan focusing on counter-terrorism in semi-urban and mountainous terrain.

questions.question: Where was the 5th edition of Exercise DUSTLIK conducted?
questions.explanation: The 5th edition of Exercise DUSTLIK was held at Termez District in the Surxondaryo Region of Uzbekistan.

questions.question: What is 'Exercise Tiger Triumph' conducted in March 2026 in Visakhapatnam and Kakinada?
options: Bilateral Tri-Services Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) exercise between India and the United States
questions.explanation: Tiger Triumph is a comprehensive Tri-Service amphibious exercise between the Indian Armed Forces and the United States military.

questions.question: Where was the foundation stone laid for India's first commercial semiconductor wafer fabrication facility (Fab) partnered by Tata Electronics and PSMC?
questions.explanation: Tata Electronics partnered with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp (PSMC) to build India's premier ₹91,000 crore semiconductor fab in Dholera Special Investment Region.

questions.question: Where is the greenfield semiconductor assembly and testing (OSAT) facility of Tata Semiconductor Assembly and Test (TSAT) being constructed?
questions.explanation: The ₹27,000 crore semiconductor packaging facility is being established at Jagiroad in Assam, marking the northeast region's first high-tech fab facility.

questions.question: Which project by CG Power in partnership with Renesas Electronics is establishing an OSAT facility in Gujarat?
questions.explanation: CG Power, Renesas (Japan), and Stars Microelectronics (Thailand) partnered to establish a commercial semiconductor packaging facility in Sanand.

questions.question: What is the total financial support approved by the Government of India under the 'Semicon India Programme'?
questions.explanation: The Semicon India Programme offers 50% fiscal support on equal terms for setting up Silicon Semiconductor Fabs, Display Fabs, and OSAT units with a ₹76,000 crore outlay.

questions.question: Which is India's fastest and most powerful AI supercomputer, installed at C-DAC Pune and ranked among the world's top 100 supercomputers?
options: AIRAWAT (AI Research Analytics and Knowledge Dissemination Platform)
questions.explanation: AIRAWAT, installed under the National AI Mission at C-DAC Pune, delivers 13,170 teraflops of AI compute and ranked among the top 100 fastest AI systems globally.

questions.question: Where is the weather supercomputing facility 'Pratyush' and 'Mihir' situated in India?
options: Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune and NCMRWF, Noida
questions.explanation: Pratyush (4 Petaflops) is located at IITM Pune and Mihir (2.8 Petaflops) at the National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF) in Noida.

questions.question: Under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM), which apex agencies oversee the deployment of indigenous 'PARAM' supercomputers?
options: Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY), implemented by C-DAC and IISc
questions.explanation: NSM is jointly steered by DST and MeitY, and executed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) and Indian Institute of Science (IISc).

questions.question: What is the name of the indigenous microprocessor series developed by IIT Madras under the Microprocessor Development Programme?
questions.explanation: The SHAKTI processor family was designed by the RISE group at IIT Madras based on the open-source RISC-V Instruction Set Architecture (ISA).

questions.question: Which microprocessor was developed indigenously by IIT Bombay?
questions.explanation: AJIT is the first microprocessor designed and conceptualized entirely by engineers and researchers at IIT Bombay.

questions.question: Which Indian Navy stealth frigate was deployed to the Gulf of Aden and Red Sea for anti-piracy and maritime security operations under 'Operation Sankalp'?
options: INS Kolkata, INS Kochi, and INS Visakhapatnam
questions.explanation: Indian Navy guided-missile destroyers INS Kolkata, INS Kochi, and INS Visakhapatnam executed daring rescue operations against Somali pirates, securing merchant ships.

questions.question: In a major anti-piracy operation 1,400 nautical miles off the Indian coast, the Indian Navy intercepted which hijacked ex-merchant ship and rescued 17 crew members?
questions.explanation: INS Kolkata, assisted by patrol vessel INS Subhadra, Sea Guardian drones, and MARCOS commandos dropped from C-17 aircraft, forced all 35 Somali pirates aboard MV Ruen to surrender.

questions.question: What is the elite special operations force of the Indian Navy called?
questions.explanation: MARCOS (officially Marine Commando Force - MCF) is the Indian Navy's specialized maritime combat and counter-terrorism unit.

questions.question: What is the special forces unit of the Indian Air Force called?
questions.explanation: The Garud Commando Force, raised in 2004, is the special operations unit of the Indian Air Force tasked with airfield defence, radar busting, and combat search & rescue.

questions.question: What is the special forces wing of the Indian Army called?
questions.explanation: The Parachute Regiment's Para SF battalions are the specialized strike commandos of the Indian Army.

questions.question: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces under Article 53(2) of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 53(2) states that the supreme command of the Defence Forces of the Union shall be vested in the President of India and the exercise thereof shall be regulated by law.

questions.question: Who is the current Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of India?
questions.explanation: General Anil Chauhan serves as the second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of India, succeeding the late General Bipin Rawat.

questions.question: Who is the current Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) of the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: General Upendra Dwivedi assumed charge as the 30th Chief of the Army Staff on June 30, 2024.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) of the Indian Navy in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Admiral Dinesh Kumar Tripathi assumed charge as the 26th Chief of the Naval Staff, succeeding Admiral R. Hari Kumar.

questions.question: Which country conducted the joint military exercise 'Nomadic Elephant' with the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: Exercise Nomadic Elephant is an annual bilateral training exercise between the Indian Army and the Mongolian Armed Forces.

questions.question: Which indigenous aircraft carrier completed all carrier integration sea trials in the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: INS Vikrant, India's first indigenously designed and constructed aircraft carrier (built by Cochin Shipyard), successfully integrated MiG-29K and LCA Navy flight operations.

questions.question: What is the ski-jump aircraft launch configuration used on INS Vikrant and INS Vikramaditya called?
questions.explanation: Both operational Indian aircraft carriers feature STOBAR configuration, using an upward-angled ski-jump bow ramp for take-off and arrester wires for landing.

questions.question: What is the proposed displacement of the planned second indigenous aircraft carrier (IAC-2) approved for repeat order?
options: Approximately 45,000 tonnes (sister ship to INS Vikrant)
questions.explanation: The Defence Acquisition Council cleared plans for a repeat order of a 45,000-tonne Vikrant-class carrier from Cochin Shipyard to ensure three operational carriers.

questions.question: Which air-to-air missile developed by DRDO has an operational range of 110+ km and travels at speeds beyond Mach 4.5?
questions.explanation: Astra Mk-1 is India's indigenous Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air Missile (BVRAAM), integrated on Su-30MKI and LCA Tejas fighters.

questions.question: What is the extended range of the advanced 'Astra Mk-2' air-to-air missile being developed by DRDO?
questions.explanation: Astra Mk-2 features an optical/RF proximity fuse and dual-pulse solid rocket motor capable of engaging aerial targets up to 160 km away.

questions.question: Which defence PSU manufactures the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas in India?
questions.explanation: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) manufactures the LCA Tejas fighter jets at its Aircraft Division facilities in Bengaluru, Karnataka.

questions.question: Which engine powers the LCA Tejas Mk-1 and Mk-1A fighter aircraft?
questions.explanation: The Tejas Mk-1 and Mk-1A are powered by the GE F404 turbofan engine, while the upcoming Tejas Mk-2 will use the higher-thrust GE F414-INS6 engine.

questions.question: Under which joint agreement will HAL and GE Aerospace co-produce the F414 jet engine in India with 80% technology transfer?
options: India-US Initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology (iCET)
questions.explanation: Under the iCET framework, the US approved full operational co-production of GE F414 engines in India with an unprecedented 80% transfer of technology.

questions.question: Which country partners with India on the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile joint venture?
questions.explanation: BrahMos Aerospace is an Indo-Russian joint venture formed in 1998, named after the Brahmaputra (India) and Moskva (Russia) rivers.

questions.question: What is the speed of the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile?
questions.explanation: BrahMos travels at Mach 2.8 (nearly three times the speed of sound), making it the world's fastest operational cruise missile.

questions.question: Which Southeast Asian country became the first export customer for India's shore-based BrahMos missile system?
questions.explanation: The Philippines acquired three batteries of the shore-based anti-ship BrahMos missile system in a $375 million export contract.

questions.question: What is the extended range of the modern BrahMos missile following India's entry into the MTCR?
questions.explanation: Following India's formal accession to the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) in 2016, BrahMos range was upgraded from 290 km to 450–500 km.

questions.question: What is 'Pralay' missile developed by DRDO for conventional battlefield strikes?
options: Short-range quasi-ballistic surface-to-surface missile with 150-500 km range
questions.explanation: Pralay is a solid-propellant battlefield missile that can change its path in mid-air to evade interceptor missiles, carrying 500-1000 kg conventional warheads.

questions.question: Which shipyard constructed the Kalvari-class (Scorpene) diesel-electric attack submarines in India under Project 75?
questions.explanation: MDL constructed all six Project 75 Scorpene submarines (Kalvari, Khanderi, Karanj, Vela, Vagir, and Vagsheer) in technology partnership with Naval Group of France.

questions.question: What is the name of the sixth and final Scorpene submarine commissioned under Project 75?
questions.explanation: INS Vagsheer (named after the sandfish) completed all rigorous weapon and sensor trials, concluding the Project 75 submarine series.

questions.question: What technology is being retrofitted onto Kalvari-class submarines by DRDO to allow them to remain submerged for extended durations?
questions.explanation: DRDO's Naval Materials Research Laboratory (NMRL) developed a fuel-cell based AIP module that enables conventional submarines to remain underwater for up to two weeks.

questions.question: Which Indian nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN) completed its deterrence patrol, solidifying India's nuclear triad?
questions.explanation: INS Arihant completed its inaugural deterrence patrol, giving India an operational, survivable second-strike nuclear capability across air, land, and sea.

questions.question: What is the name of India's second nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN) commissioned at Visakhapatnam?
questions.explanation: INS Arighaat was formally commissioned into the Strategic Forces Command in August 2024 at Visakhapatnam, enhancing strategic deterrence.

questions.question: Which submarine-launched ballistic missile (SLBM) is carried by INS Arihant?
options: K-15 Sagarika (range ~750 km) and K-4 (range ~3,500 km)
questions.explanation: The 'K' family of SLBMs (named after Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam) includes K-15 (Sagarika) and the advanced K-4 missile.

questions.question: What is India's official nuclear doctrine adopted in 2003 regarding the use of nuclear weapons?
options: No First Use (NFU) and Credible Minimum Deterrence
questions.explanation: India's nuclear doctrine maintains 'No First Use' against nuclear states and non-use against non-nuclear states, with guaranteed massive punitive second-strike retaliation.

questions.question: Who is the Chairman of the Political Council of the Nuclear Command Authority (NCA) of India?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister chairs the Political Council of the NCA, which is the sole authority that can authorize the operational use of nuclear weapons.

questions.question: Who heads the Executive Council of the Nuclear Command Authority (NCA)?
questions.explanation: The National Security Advisor (NSA) chairs the Executive Council, which provides inputs to the Political Council and executes directives issued by it.

questions.question: Who is the current National Security Advisor (NSA) of India?
questions.explanation: Ajit Doval was re-appointed as the National Security Advisor for a historic third term with the rank of a Union Cabinet Minister.

questions.question: National Technology Day is observed in India every year on May 11 to celebrate which historic event?
options: Pokhran-II nuclear tests (Operation Shakti) conducted on May 11, 1998
questions.explanation: National Technology Day commemorates the successful underground nuclear tests in Pokhran on May 11, 1998, as well as the maiden flight of the indigenous Hansa-3 aircraft.

questions.question: Which indigenously developed anti-radiation missile was successfully test-fired by DRDO from a Su-30MKI fighter?
questions.explanation: Rudram is India's first indigenous New Generation Anti-Radiation Missile (NGARM) designed to neutralize enemy surveillance radars and tracking stations.

questions.question: What is the primary role of an 'Anti-Radiation Missile' like Rudram?
options: To track and home in on enemy radar transmissions, air defence systems, and communication emitters
To intercept ballistic missiles in space
questions.explanation: Anti-radiation missiles use passive homing heads to locate radio-frequency and microwave emissions from hostile radar and jamming installations.

questions.question: Which air-to-surface anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) was developed by DRDO for integration on ALH Dhruv and LCH Prachand helicopters?
questions.explanation: HELINA (army version) and Dhruvastra (air force version) are third-generation fire-and-forget ATGMs equipped with imaging infrared (IIR) seekers.

questions.question: What is the operational strike range of the HELINA anti-tank guided missile?
questions.explanation: HELINA can engage battlefield targets from a standoff distance of up to 7-8 km in direct hit and top-attack modes.

questions.question: Which Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) developed by HAL is the world's only attack helicopter capable of landing and taking off at an altitude of 5,000 metres?
questions.explanation: LCH Prachand, inducted by the Army and IAF, is engineered specifically for high-altitude combat in Siachen and eastern Ladakh.

questions.question: Which multi-role combat helicopter was developed as the armed weaponized version of HAL's Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH Dhruv)?
questions.explanation: HAL Rudra is the Weapon System Integrated (WSI) variant of the ALH Dhruv, fitted with 20mm turret guns, 70mm rockets, and Mistral missiles.

questions.question: Which foreign aerospace major manufactures the Apache AH-64E attack helicopters acquired by the Indian Air Force and Indian Army?
questions.explanation: Boeing manufactures the AH-64E Apache Guardian, with fuselages produced by Tata Boeing Aerospace Limited (TBAL) in Hyderabad.

questions.question: Where is Tata Boeing Aerospace Limited (TBAL) facility located in India?
questions.explanation: TBAL operates its advanced aerospace manufacturing facility at Adibatla in Hyderabad, producing AH-64 Apache fuselages for global customers.

questions.question: Which military aircraft manufacturer produces the C-295 medium tactical transport aircraft for the Indian Air Force?
options: Airbus Defence and Space in partnership with Tata Advanced Systems (TASL)
questions.explanation: Airbus and Tata Advanced Systems established India's first private sector military aircraft Final Assembly Line (FAL) in Vadodara, Gujarat.

questions.question: Where was the Final Assembly Line (FAL) plant for C-295 transport aircraft inaugurated in Gujarat?
questions.explanation: The C-295 FAL in Vadodara will manufacture 40 of the 56 contracted aircraft, creating an indigenous defense aerospace manufacturing hub.

questions.question: What aircraft did the Airbus C-295 primarily replace in the Indian Air Force fleet?
questions.explanation: The 5-10 tonne capacity C-295 aircraft replaces the legacy fleet of British-origin Avro-748 transport planes in service since the 1960s.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the 'DRDO SMART' system successfully test-fired off the coast of Odisha in May 2026?
options: Supersonic Missile Assisted Release of Torpedo (long-range anti-submarine warfare)
questions.explanation: SMART is a canisterized hybrid missile system that delivers a lightweight torpedo at supersonic speeds over 600 km to engage enemy submarines.

questions.question: Which lightweight torpedo is integrated into the SMART missile system?
questions.explanation: SMART carries the indigenous TAL Shyena lightweight torpedo, parachuted into the water in the vicinity of target coordinates.

questions.question: What is 'Varunastra' developed by DRDO and manufactured by Bharat Dynamics Limited?
options: Ship-launched, electrically propelled Heavyweight Anti-Submarine Torpedo
questions.explanation: Varunastra is a state-of-the-art 1.5-tonne heavyweight anti-submarine torpedo capable of striking quiet submarines in deep and shallow waters at 40 knots.

questions.question: Which indigenous long-range glide bomb was test-fired by DRDO from a Sukhoi-30MKI fighter in May 2026?
questions.explanation: DRDO conducted successful flight tests of 'Gaurav', a 1,000 kg class winged glide bomb using GPS/NavIC satellite guidance with a 100 km standoff range.

questions.question: What is 'SAAW' developed by DRDO for airfield neutralization?
questions.explanation: SAAW is a 125 kg high-precision guided stand-off glide bomb designed to destroy ground targets like runways, bunkers, and aircraft hangars up to 100 km away.

questions.question: What is India's indigenous satellite navigation system developed by ISRO called?
questions.explanation: NavIC is an autonomous regional satellite navigation system covering India and an area extending 1,500 km around its borders.

questions.question: How many satellites constitute the operational baseline constellation of NavIC (IRNSS)?
options: 7 satellites (3 in geostationary orbit, 4 in geosynchronous orbit)
questions.explanation: NavIC uses a constellation of 7 satellites: 3 in Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) at 32.5°E, 83°E, and 129.5°E, and 4 in inclined Geosynchronous Orbit (GSO).

questions.question: What frequency bands does the second-generation NavIC satellite series (NVS) utilize?
questions.explanation: NVS series satellites incorporate the interoperable L1 civilian band (1575.42 MHz) alongside L5 and S bands, making NavIC accessible in commercial smartphones.

questions.question: What atomic clock technology is incorporated aboard the indigenous NVS-01 navigation satellite?
options: Indigenous Rubidium Atomic Clock developed by Space Applications Centre (SAC) Ahmedabad
questions.explanation: NVS-01 is powered by an indigenous space-qualified rubidium atomic frequency standard developed by ISRO's SAC in Ahmedabad.

questions.question: What is 'GAGAN' developed jointly by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India (AAI)?
options: GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation (Satellite-Based Augmentation System - SBAS)
questions.explanation: GAGAN provides seamless, precision satellite-guided navigation over Indian airspace for civil aviation, making India the fourth nation with operational SBAS.

questions.question: Which was the first commercial airline in Asia to use GAGAN satellite-based technology for landing an aircraft?
questions.explanation: IndiGo successfully landed an ATR-72 aircraft at Kishangarh using the Localizer Performance with Vertical Guidance (LPV) approach powered by GAGAN.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Airports Authority of India (AAI) located?
options: Rajiv Gandhi Bhawan, Safdarjung Airport, New Delhi
questions.explanation: AAI, a statutory body under the Ministry of Civil Aviation, is headquartered at Rajiv Gandhi Bhawan in New Delhi.

questions.question: What is 'Bhuvan' developed by ISRO?
options: A national Geoportal providing multi-sensor satellite imagery and spatial data services
questions.explanation: Bhuvan is ISRO's indigenous web-based 2D and 3D GIS platform providing earth observation data, natural disaster maps, and governance planning layers.

questions.question: ISRO unveiled the design architecture for the first module of the 'Bharatiya Antariksh Station' (BAS-1). What is the targeted launch year for BAS-1?
questions.explanation: ISRO plans to launch BAS-1 (a 52-tonne space station module) by 2028, with the complete multi-module space station operational by 2035, ahead of a planned crewed lunar landing by 2040.

questions.question: By which target year has India set the national goal to land an Indian astronaut on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi set two visionary space milestones: setting up the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and landing an Indian astronaut on the Moon by 2040.

questions.question: What is the name of the next-generation heavy launch vehicle being developed by ISRO to support the Moon landing and space station modules?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved development of the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV, named 'Soorya'), featuring semi-cryogenic and reusable methane-liquid oxygen stages.

questions.question: What payload capacity to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) is the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) designed to deliver in its reusable configuration?
questions.explanation: NGLV will deliver up to 30 tonnes to LEO in expendable mode and around 20 tonnes in reusable booster mode, three times the capacity of LVM3.

questions.question: Which multi-nation air combat exercise, the largest ever conducted on Indian soil, was scheduled by the Indian Air Force in two phases in mid-2026?
questions.explanation: Exercise Tarang Shakti brought together air forces from over 30 countries at Sulur (Tamil Nadu) and Jodhpur (Rajasthan) with fighter jets from Germany, France, UK, and US.

questions.question: Which European nation deployed Eurofighter Typhoons to India for the first time to participate in Exercise Tarang Shakti?
questions.explanation: The German Air Force deployed Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jets and A400M transport aircraft to India for the inaugural phase of Tarang Shakti.

questions.question: Where was the joint military exercise 'MAITREE' between the Indian Army and the Royal Thai Army conducted?
questions.explanation: Exercise MAITREE 2026 was conducted at the Fort Vachiraprakan in Tak Province, Thailand, focusing on counter-insurgency and counter-terror tactics.

questions.question: Which bilateral naval exercise is conducted annually between the Indian Navy and the French Navy?
questions.explanation: Varuna is the bilateral maritime exercise between the Indian and French navies. (Shakti is the army exercise, and Garuda is the air force exercise).

questions.question: What is the name of the bilateral army exercise conducted between India and France?
questions.explanation: Exercise SHAKTI is the joint military exercise conducted between the Indian Army and the French Army.

questions.question: What is the joint military exercise conducted between the Indian Army and the Singapore Army called?
options: Both Bold Kurukshetra and Agni Warrior
questions.explanation: India and Singapore conduct Exercise Bold Kurukshetra (armour/infantry) and Exercise Agni Warrior (artillery), while SIMBEX is their bilateral naval exercise.

questions.question: What does 'SIMBEX' stand for in bilateral defence engagements?
questions.explanation: SIMBEX is the annual maritime warfare exercise conducted between the Indian Navy and the Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN) since 1994.

questions.question: Which bilateral naval exercise is conducted between the Indian Navy and the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Exercise Konkan is the annual naval drill between India and the UK. (Ajeya Warrior is their army exercise, and Indradhanush is their air exercise).

questions.question: What is the name of the annual bilateral military exercise between the Indian Army and the British Army?
questions.explanation: Exercise Ajeya Warrior is the biennial joint army training exercise between India and the United Kingdom.

questions.question: Which joint military exercise is conducted between India and Oman?
options: Exercise AL NAJAH (Army), NASEEM AL BAHR (Navy), EASTERN BRIDGE (Air Force)
questions.explanation: India and Oman conduct tripartite cooperation: Al Najah (Army), Naseem Al Bahr (Navy), and Eastern Bridge (Air Force).

questions.question: Which bilateral military exercise is conducted between India and Japan?
options: DHARMA GUARDIAN (Army), JIMEX (Navy), SHINYUU MAITRI (Air Force)
questions.explanation: India-Japan defense cooperation spans Dharma Guardian (Army), JIMEX (Navy), Shinyuu Maitri (transport aircraft), and Veer Guardian (fighter jets).

questions.question: What is the bilateral army exercise between India and the United States known as?
options: Both Yudh Abhyas and Vajra Prahar
questions.explanation: Yudh Abhyas is the battalion-level conventional warfare exercise, while Vajra Prahar is the specialized joint training between Indian and US Special Forces.

questions.question: Which multinational air combat exercise is hosted biennially by the Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) in Darwin, where the IAF participates?
questions.explanation: Exercise Pitch Black is Australia's premier multilateral air warfare exercise in the Northern Territory, featuring complex night-flying and strike simulations.

questions.question: What is 'Deep Ocean Mission' (Samudrayaan) approved by the Ministry of Earth Sciences?
options: A mission to explore deep-sea resources and develop a 3-person submersible 'Matsya 6000' to reach 6,000 metres depth
questions.explanation: The Samudrayaan project under the Deep Ocean Mission develops an indigenous human submersible (Matsya-6000) to carry 3 scientists to a depth of 6 km for polymetallic nodules exploration.

questions.question: Which institute developed the 'Matsya 6000' human submersible under the Deep Ocean Mission?
options: National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai
National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa
questions.explanation: NIOT in Chennai designed the titanium alloy manned sphere and sub-systems for the Matsya-6000 deep-sea submersible.

questions.question: Where is the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR) located?
questions.explanation: NCPOR is the premier R&D institution under the Ministry of Earth Sciences located in Goa, managing India's Antarctic and Arctic research stations.

questions.question: What are the names of India's active permanent research stations in Antarctica?
questions.explanation: India's active scientific research bases in Antarctica are Maitri (commissioned 1989) and Bharati (commissioned 2012). (Dakshin Gangotri was decommissioned in 1990).

questions.question: What is the name of India's permanent research station in the Arctic, established in 2008 at Ny-Alesund, Svalbard, Norway?
questions.explanation: Himadri is India's dedicated Arctic research station located at the International Arctic Research base in Spitsbergen, Svalbard, Norway.

questions.question: What is 'IndARC' deployed by India in the Arctic Ocean?
options: India's first multi-sensor moored underwater observatory in Kongsfjorden, Svalbard
questions.explanation: IndARC is an underwater oceanographic observatory moored at 192 metres depth in the Arctic fjord to monitor Arctic climate impact on the Indian monsoon.

questions.question: What is the name of the research station operated by India in the high Himalayas at Chandra Basin, Himachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Himansh is India's high-altitude research station established by NCPOR at Sutri Dhaka in the Chandra basin (Spiti valley) to study Himalayan glaciology.

questions.question: Under which statutory Act is the legal framework for Indian activities in Antarctica governed?
questions.explanation: The Indian Antarctic Act, 2022 provides a comprehensive domestic legal framework to protect the Antarctic environment and regulate Indian research expeditions.

questions.question: ISRO announced the multi-module mission profile of 'Chandrayaan-4'. What is the primary objective of the Chandrayaan-4 mission?
options: Lunar Sample Return Mission (collecting lunar soil samples and returning them safely to Earth)
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-4 is a complex 5-module lunar sample-return mission that will collect core samples near the lunar south pole, dock in lunar orbit, and return them to Earth.

questions.question: How many spacecraft modules make up the Chandrayaan-4 mission architecture across two rocket launches?
options: 5 modules (Propulsion, Lander, Ascender, Transfer, and Re-entry Module)
questions.explanation: The architecture involves two LVM3 launches carrying 5 integrated modules: Lander Module, Ascender Module, Transfer Module, Re-entry Module, and Propulsion Module.

questions.question: What is 'LUPEX' (Lunar Polar Exploration) mission planned jointly by ISRO and JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency)?
options: A joint mission to send a lunar rover and lander to explore water ice in the permanently shadowed regions of the Moon's south pole
questions.explanation: LUPEX is an Indo-Japanese joint lunar mission where JAXA provides the rocket and rover, while ISRO develops the lander system to prospect for water ice.

questions.question: Which Earth Observation Satellite was launched by ISRO aboard SSLV-D3 in its final developmental flight in mid-2026?
questions.explanation: ISRO successfully launched the Earth Observation Satellite EOS-08 aboard the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV-D3) from Sriharikota, operationalizing the rocket.

questions.question: What three primary payloads are carried by ISRO's EOS-08 microsatellite?
options: Electro-Optical Infrared (EOIR), Global Navigation Satellite System-Reflectometry (GNSS-R), and SiC UV Dosimeter
questions.explanation: EOS-08 features EOIR for thermal/wildfire monitoring, GNSS-R for ocean surface wind and soil moisture measurement, and a Silicon Carbide UV Dosimeter for Gaganyaan crew safety.

questions.question: What milestone did the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) achieve with the successful SSLV-D3 launch?
options: Successful completion of the SSLV Development Programme, paving the way for commercial production by Indian industry / NSIL
questions.explanation: SSLV-D3 marked the full operationalization of the launcher, enabling NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) to license technology to private industrial consortia.

questions.question: What is the commercial arm of ISRO incorporated under the administrative control of the Department of Space?
questions.explanation: NSIL, incorporated in 2019, is the central public sector commercial entity responsible for marketing ISRO space products, building satellites, and operating commercial launch services.

questions.question: What is the single-window nodal agency established to authorize, facilitate, and supervise space activities of non-government private entities (NGEs) in India?
options: IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre)
questions.explanation: IN-SPACe acts as an autonomous single-window regulator and promoter for private space companies, startups, and academic institutions in India.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of IN-SPACe located?
questions.explanation: The headquarters of IN-SPACe were inaugurated by Prime Minister Modi at Bopal in Ahmedabad.

questions.question: Which private Indian space-tech startup launched 'Agnibaan SOrTeD', India's first rocket powered by a single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine?
questions.explanation: Chennai-based startup Agnikul Cosmos achieved the milestone launch of Agnibaan SOrTeD from India's first private launchpad (ALP-1) at Sriharikota.

questions.question: What is the name of the world's first single-piece 3D-printed rocket engine developed by Agnikul Cosmos?
questions.explanation: Agnilet is an indigenous semi-cryogenic rocket engine 3D-printed in one single piece using Inconel superalloy, eliminating hundreds of welded joints.

questions.question: Which was the first private Indian company to launch a privately developed rocket ('Vikram-S') into space in 2022 under Mission Prarambh?
questions.explanation: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace made history on November 18, 2022, by launching the sub-orbital rocket Vikram-S from ISRO's spaceport at Sriharikota.

questions.question: Which Indian startup is launching a constellation of hyperspectral imaging satellites named 'Fireflies'?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru-based space-tech startup Pixxel is deploying hyperspectral imaging satellites to detect gas leaks, crop diseases, and mining illegalities.

questions.question: What is 'Aditya-L1' launched by ISRO to study the Sun, and around which point in space is it halo-orbiting?
options: Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1), approximately 1.5 million km from Earth
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 was successfully inserted into a halo orbit around the first Lagrangian point (L1), providing an uninterrupted 24x7 view of the Sun without eclipses.

questions.question: What are the primary solar instruments aboard Aditya-L1 for observing the solar corona and chromosphere?
options: VELC (Visible Emission Line Coronagraph) and SUIT (Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope)
questions.explanation: VELC (developed by Indian Institute of Astrophysics Bengaluru) and SUIT (developed by IUCAA Pune) observe solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and space weather.

questions.question: What is 'XPoSat' (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) launched by ISRO in 2024?
options: India's first dedicated polarimetry mission to study the dynamics of bright astronomical X-ray sources in extreme conditions
questions.explanation: XPoSat is only the world's second satellite-based X-ray polarimetry mission (after NASA's IXPE), carrying POLIX and XSPECT payloads built with Raman Research Institute.

questions.question: What is 'NISAR' satellite developed jointly by NASA and ISRO?
options: NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (dual-frequency L-band and S-band radar satellite for global land and ice deformation monitoring)
questions.explanation: NISAR is an advanced Earth-observing satellite featuring dual-frequency SweepSAR technology (L-band from NASA, S-band from ISRO) to track natural hazards and ecosystem changes.

questions.question: Where is the Satellite Integration and Test Facility for the NISAR satellite located ahead of launch aboard GSLV?
options: U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC), Bengaluru
questions.explanation: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) shipped the L-band radar payload to URSC in Bengaluru, where ISRO completed integration with the S-band payload and satellite bus.

questions.question: Which organization operates the Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN) antennas at Byalalu near Bengaluru for communicating with lunar and interplanetary probes?
options: ISRO Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC)
questions.explanation: ISTRAC manages the 18m and 32m deep-space antennas at Byalalu, tracking Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan, and Aditya-L1 missions across deep space.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) situated in Hyderabad?
options: Acquisition, processing, and dissemination of satellite data from remote sensing satellites
questions.explanation: NRSC in Hyderabad is ISRO's lead center for satellite data acquisition from Indian and foreign remote sensing constellations, operating ground stations at Shadnagar.

questions.question: Where is the Master Control Facility (MCF) of ISRO located, which monitors and controls geostationary satellites?
questions.explanation: ISRO's MCF operates two stations at Hassan in Karnataka (established 1982) and Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh (established 2005) for round-the-clock geostationary orbit operations.

questions.question: Where is the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) situated, serving as the lead center for launch vehicle design and development?
questions.explanation: VSSC at Thumba, Thiruvananthapuram, is ISRO's premier center for rocket technology, responsible for PSLV, GSLV, and LVM3 launch vehicles.

questions.question: Where is the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) located, where high-thrust cryogenic engines and stages are tested?
questions.explanation: IPRC Mahendragiri houses state-of-the-art testing complexes for liquid engines (Vikas, CE-7.5, CE-20) and high-altitude simulation facilities.

questions.question: Where is the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC) of ISRO headquartered?
questions.explanation: LPSC is the center for design and development of liquid and cryogenic propulsion stages, with facilities at Valiamala in Kerala and Bengaluru in Karnataka.

questions.question: Where is the Space Applications Centre (SAC) of ISRO located, specializing in communication and optical/microwave imaging sensors?
questions.explanation: SAC in Ahmedabad designs communication payloads, transponders, meteorological cameras, and synthetic aperture radars for ISRO satellites.

questions.question: On which date was National Space Day celebrated for the second/third time across India, commemorating the historic soft landing of Chandrayaan-3?
questions.explanation: National Space Day is celebrated annually on August 23 to commemorate the soft landing of Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander on the lunar surface on August 23, 2023.

questions.question: What was the official theme for National Space Day 2026?
options: Touching Lives while Touching the Moon: India's Space Saga
questions.explanation: The theme highlighted the dual dimension of space exploration: planetary milestones and societal benefits like disaster management, agriculture, and communication.

questions.question: What is the official name given to the Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing site near the lunar south pole?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi named the touchdown point of Chandrayaan-3's lander as 'Shiv Shakti Point'.

questions.question: What was the impact point of Chandrayaan-2's Vikram lander in 2019 named as?
questions.explanation: The location where Chandrayaan-2 crash-landed on the Moon in September 2019 was designated as 'Tiranga Point'.
