questions.question: What was the impact site of Chandrayaan-1's Moon Impact Probe (MIP) in November 2008 named as?
questions.explanation: The Moon Impact Probe touched down near Shackleton Crater on November 14, 2008 (Jawaharlal Nehru's birth anniversary), and the site was named 'Jawahar Point'.

questions.question: Which rover was deployed by Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander to conduct in-situ chemical and elemental analysis of lunar regolith?
questions.explanation: The 26 kg, 6-wheeled Pragyan rover rolled down Vikram's ramp, travelling over 100 metres and discovering sulfur on the lunar surface using its LIBS payload.

questions.question: What payload aboard Chandrayaan-3's Pragyan rover confirmed the presence of Sulfur (S) on the lunar surface near the south pole?
questions.explanation: The LIBS instrument, developed by Laboratory for Electro-Optics Systems (LEOS) Bengaluru, confirmed unambiguous sulfur signatures in lunar soil.

questions.question: What was the scientific objective of the 'ChaSTE' (Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment) payload on the Vikram lander?
options: To measure the thermal conductivity and temperature gradient of lunar topsoil up to 10 cm depth
questions.explanation: ChaSTE recorded a sharp temperature difference between the surface (around 50°C) and 8 cm underneath (-10°C), demonstrating the high insulating properties of lunar regolith.

questions.question: Which instrument aboard the Vikram lander recorded lunar seismic activity and vibrations generated by Pragyan rover movements?
questions.explanation: ILSA, a micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) based seismometer developed by LEOS, detected lunar ground movements and micro-tremors.

questions.question: What unexpected milestone did ISRO achieve with the Vikram lander before the onset of the lunar night?
options: A successful hop experiment (firing engines to elevate 40 cm and landing safely 30-40 cm away)
questions.explanation: The successful hop test demonstrated restartable thruster capabilities and vertical takeoff, vital for future sample-return and human lunar missions.

questions.question: What is the primary role of DRDO's Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle (HSTDV)?
options: To demonstrate autonomous scramjet engine flight at speeds exceeding Mach 6 in the atmosphere
questions.explanation: HSTDV is an unmanned scramjet demonstration aircraft capable of cruising at Mach 6 (over 2 km per second) using atmospheric oxygen for combustion.

questions.question: What type of air-breathing engine operates efficiently only at hypersonic speeds (above Mach 5) by combusting fuel in supersonic airflow?
questions.explanation: Unlike turbojets or ramjets that decelerate intake air to subsonic speeds, a scramjet combusts fuel directly in supersonic airflow, enabling sustained hypersonic flight.

questions.question: What is 'Project Kusha' being undertaken by DRDO for the Indian Air Force?
options: Indigenous Long-Range Surface-to-Air Defence Missile System (LR-SAM) with 350-400 km interception range, comparable to S-400
questions.explanation: Project Kusha will field a three-tier surface-to-air missile system capable of taking down stealth fighters, cruise missiles, precision-guided munitions, and ballistic missiles up to 350 km away.

questions.question: From which country did India procure the 'S-400 Triumf' air defence missile squadrons?
questions.explanation: India signed a $5.43 billion contract with Russia in 2018 for five squadrons of the advanced S-400 Triumf long-range surface-to-air missile system.

questions.question: What is the operational designation given by the Indian Air Force to the deployed S-400 air defence missile systems?
questions.explanation: The Indian Air Force named its deployed S-400 missile systems 'Sudarshan', invoking Lord Krishna's mythical defensive weapon.

questions.question: Which air base in Punjab received the first deployed squadron of the S-400 Sudarshan system to protect the northern and western skies?
options: Halwara and Pathankot / Adampur air base sector
questions.explanation: The first S-400 squadron was deployed along the Punjab sector to counter aerial threats across the western border.

questions.question: Which French fighter aircraft are operated by the Indian Air Force's Golden Arrows (No. 17 Squadron) at Ambala?
questions.explanation: The IAF operates 36 Dassault Rafale 4.5-generation multi-role combat aircraft based at Ambala (No. 17 Golden Arrows) and Hasimara (No. 101 Falcons).

questions.question: What long-range air-to-air missile gives the Rafale fighter unmatched beyond-visual-range combat superiority?
options: Meteor Missile (ramjet powered with 150+ km range)
questions.explanation: The Meteor missile, powered by a solid-fuel variable-flow ducted ramjet, has a 'no-escape zone' more than three times greater than conventional air-to-air missiles.

questions.question: What is the stealth stand-off deep strike cruise missile carried by the IAF's Rafale aircraft?
questions.explanation: SCALP is a long-range, air-launched, precision-guided cruise missile capable of striking hardened underground bunkers and high-value strategic targets.

questions.question: What precision-guided munition kit fitted on Rafale aircraft was rapidly acquired by India for high-altitude bunker busting?
options: HAMMER (Highly Agile Modular Munition Extended Range)
questions.explanation: AASM Hammer is a rocket-assisted, modular precision standoff guidance kit produced by Safran, adaptable to various bomb bodies.

questions.question: Which DRDO laboratory in Hyderabad is the nodal center for the design and development of missile systems including Agni and Prithvi?
options: All of the above (part of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Missile Complex)
questions.explanation: The Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Missile Complex in Hyderabad comprises DRDL, RCI (founded by Kalam for avionics and navigation), and ASL (propulsion and composites).

questions.question: Who founded the Research Centre Imarat (RCI) in Hyderabad in 1988 to spearhead indigenous missile guidance and navigation systems?
questions.explanation: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam conceptualized and founded RCI as a world-class avionics and seeker development laboratory under the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP).

questions.question: Which five missile systems were developed under the historic Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) launched in 1983?
options: PATNA: Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Nag, and Akash
questions.explanation: IGMDP, steered by Dr. Kalam, successfully developed the 'PATNA' missiles: Prithvi (surface-to-surface), Agni (re-entry ballistic), Trishul (short SAM), Nag (anti-tank), and Akash (medium SAM).

questions.question: What is 'Pinaka' developed by DRDO and in service with the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: Pinaka is an indigenous all-weather multi-barrel rocket artillery system that can fire a salvo of 12 HE rockets in 44 seconds, with guided versions reaching up to 75-90 km.

questions.question: Which European nation placed a major defense export order to procure indigenous Pinaka multi-barrel rocket systems from India?
questions.explanation: Armenia signed landmark government-to-government defense contracts to procure indigenous Pinaka rocket systems, Swathi radars, and ammunition from Indian manufacturers.

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was invited as the Guest of Honour at the World Government Summit 2026 held in which city?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the World Government Summit in Dubai as the Guest of Honour, emphasizing the theme 'Shaping Future Governments'.

questions.question: Where was the first traditional stone Hindu temple in the Middle East—the BAPS Hindu Mandir—inaugurated by PM Modi in February 2026?
questions.explanation: The historic BAPS Hindu Mandir built on 27 acres of land gifted by UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan was consecrated at Abu Mreikhah in Abu Dhabi.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 13th Ministerial Conference (MC13) of the World Trade Organization (WTO) in February 2026?
questions.explanation: The WTO MC13 was held in Abu Dhabi under the chairmanship of UAE Minister of State for Foreign Trade Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi.

questions.question: Who is the Director-General of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
questions.explanation: Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria is the first woman and first African to serve as the Director-General of the World Trade Organization.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO) located?
questions.explanation: The WTO, established on January 1, 1995, pursuant to the 1994 Marrakesh Agreement, is headquartered at the Centre William Rappard in Geneva.

questions.question: Which international security conference held its 60th/62nd annual session in February 2026, often described as the 'Davos of Defence'?
questions.explanation: The Munich Security Conference is the world's leading forum for debating international security policy, held annually at the Hotel Bayerischer Hof in Munich, Germany.

questions.question: Which country held the rotating G20 Presidency during 2024, leading into the G20 Sherpa and foreign ministers meetings?
questions.explanation: Brazil held the G20 Presidency under the theme 'Building a Just World and a Sustainable Planet', succeeded by South Africa.

questions.question: What is the 'Troika' in G20 terminology?
options: The grouping consisting of the previous, current, and incoming G20 Presidencies
The heads of IMF, World Bank, and WTO
questions.explanation: The G20 Troika represents continuity in governance and consists of the previous host country (India), current host (Brazil), and next host (South Africa).

questions.question: Which continental body was formally inducted as a permanent member of the G20 during the New Delhi Summit in 2023 under India's Presidency?
questions.explanation: The 55-nation African Union was formally inducted as a permanent member of the G20 at the historic New Delhi Summit under Prime Minister Modi.

questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of the African Union Commission?
questions.explanation: Moussa Faki Mahamat of Chad serves as the Chairperson of the African Union Commission, headquartered in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

questions.question: Where are the permanent headquarters of the African Union (AU) located?
questions.explanation: The African Union was established in 2002 (replacing the Organization of African Unity) and is based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

questions.question: Which country officially joined the NATO alliance in early 2024 as its 32nd member, completing its historic accession process?
questions.explanation: Sweden formally became the 32nd member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) after depositing its instrument of accession in Washington, following Finland's accession as the 31st member.

questions.question: Who serves as the Secretary General of NATO, succeeding Jens Stoltenberg in 2024?
options: Mark Rutte (former Prime Minister of the Netherlands)
questions.explanation: Former Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte was unanimously appointed as the new Secretary General of NATO, taking office in October 2024.

questions.question: Where are the political headquarters of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) located?
questions.explanation: NATO's political headquarters are located on Boulevard Léopold III in Brussels, Belgium.

questions.question: Which bilateral payment linkage was launched between India and Sri Lanka and Mauritius via virtual ceremony in February 2026?
options: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and RuPay card services
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Modi, Sri Lankan President Ranil Wickremesinghe, and Mauritian PM Pravind Jugnauth launched UPI and RuPay connectivity in Sri Lanka and Mauritius.

questions.question: On which island did India inaugurate a newly upgraded airstrip and marine jetty constructed under bilateral grant assistance with Mauritius?
questions.explanation: India and Mauritius jointly inaugurated the 3,000-metre airstrip and St. James Jetty on North Agalega Island to enhance maritime domain awareness.

questions.question: Which country withdrew its military personnel operating civilian medical helicopters in the Maldives following a request by President Mohamed Muizzu?
options: India (replaced by Indian civilian technical teams)
questions.explanation: India agreed to replace active military personnel operating two ALH Dhruv helicopters and a Dornier aircraft in the Maldives with competent civilian technical operators.

questions.question: What is the capital city of the Maldives?
questions.explanation: Male is the densely populated capital city and financial hub of the Republic of Maldives.

questions.question: Which international organization publishes the annual 'Corruption Perceptions Index' (CPI)?
questions.explanation: Berlin-based global civil society organization Transparency International publishes the annual Corruption Perceptions Index ranking 180 countries.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of Transparency International located?
questions.explanation: Transparency International was founded in 1993 and is headquartered in Berlin, Germany.

questions.question: Which country consistently ranks first (least corrupt) in Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index?
questions.explanation: Denmark has maintained the top ranking for several consecutive years as the country perceived to have the cleanest public sector.

questions.question: What is the name of the naval exercise conducted in the Arabian Sea under the Combined Maritime Forces (CMF) coalition in which Indian Navy participates as an associate/full partner?
questions.explanation: The Combined Maritime Forces (CMF), based in Bahrain, coordinates multinational maritime security and counter-piracy patrols across the Western Indian Ocean.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the United States Fifth Fleet located?
questions.explanation: The United States Naval Forces Central Command / Fifth Fleet is based at Naval Support Activity Bahrain in Manama.

questions.question: Which body within the United Nations has the primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security under Article 24 of the UN Charter?
questions.explanation: The UN Security Council has primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security and is the only UN organ with authority to issue binding resolutions.

questions.question: How many permanent and non-permanent members comprise the United Nations Security Council (UNSC)?
options: 15 members (5 permanent members: US, UK, France, Russia, China; and 10 non-permanent members elected for 2-year terms)
questions.explanation: The UNSC consists of 5 veto-wielding permanent members (P5) and 10 non-permanent members elected by the General Assembly for staggered two-year mandates.

questions.question: The 9th/10th edition of the 'Raisina Dialogue', India's premier conference on geopolitics and geo-economics, was held in New Delhi in March. Who was the Chief Guest and Keynote Speaker?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister of Greece Kyriakos Mitsotakis was the Chief Guest at the Raisina Dialogue, organized by the Observer Research Foundation (ORF) in partnership with MEA.

questions.question: What was the overarching theme of the Raisina Dialogue 2026?
questions.explanation: The theme 'Chaturanga: Conflict, Contest, Cooperate, Create' explored evolving global balance of power and emerging security architectures.

questions.question: India signed a historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) in March 2026 with which European intergovernmental organization, unlocking a commitment of $100 billion in investment?
options: EFTA (European Free Trade Association comprising Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland)
questions.explanation: India signed the TEPA with EFTA, marking the first time in an Indian trade pact that partner countries legally committed to investing $100 billion over 15 years to generate 1 million direct jobs.

questions.question: Which four nations comprise the European Free Trade Association (EFTA)?
questions.explanation: EFTA was founded in 1960 and consists of four non-EU European countries: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) located?
questions.explanation: The EFTA Secretariat is located in Geneva, Switzerland, with additional offices in Brussels and Luxembourg.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 6th NSA-Level Meeting of the 'Colombo Security Conclave' (CSC) in March 2026?
questions.explanation: Mauritius hosted the meeting, with member states (India, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, and Maldives) signing the Founding Charter and MoU establishing the permanent CSC Secretariat in Colombo.

questions.question: Which country officially signed the CSC Charter in 2024 to become the 5th full member of the Colombo Security Conclave?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh joined the regional security grouping as its fifth full member alongside India, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, and Maldives (with Seychelles as observer).

questions.question: What are the five core pillars of cooperation under the Colombo Security Conclave?
options: Maritime safety, counter-terrorism, combating trafficking, cyber security, and critical infrastructure protection
questions.explanation: CSC focuses on: 1) Maritime Safety & Security, 2) Countering Terrorism & Radicalization, 3) Combating Trafficking & Transnational Crime, 4) Cyber Security & Critical Infrastructure, and 5) HADR.

questions.question: Who is the current Secretary-General of the United Nations, serving his second five-year term?
options: Antonio Guterres (former Prime Minister of Portugal)
questions.explanation: Antonio Guterres was appointed as the ninth Secretary-General of the United Nations by the General Assembly in 2017 and was re-elected for a second term commencing January 2022.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the United Nations situated?
questions.explanation: The official world headquarters of the United Nations is an international zone located along First Avenue in Manhattan, New York City.

questions.question: Where is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations—the International Court of Justice (ICJ)—located?
options: The Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands
questions.explanation: The ICJ is the only one of the six principal organs of the United Nations not located in New York City, holding its seat at the Peace Palace in The Hague.

questions.question: How many judges serve on the International Court of Justice (ICJ), and what is their term of office?
options: 15 judges elected for 9-year terms by the UN General Assembly and Security Council
questions.explanation: The ICJ consists of 15 judges elected for nine-year terms, with one-third of the court (5 judges) retiring every three years.

questions.question: Who is the sitting Indian judge at the International Court of Justice (ICJ)?
questions.explanation: Justice Dalveer Bhandari was first elected to the ICJ in 2012 and was re-elected in 2017 for a second full nine-year term ending in 2027.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to serve as the President of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)?
questions.explanation: Dr. Nagendra Singh served as a Judge at the ICJ from 1973 and was elected as its President from 1985 to 1988.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 3rd Summit for Democracy in March 2026?
questions.explanation: South Korea hosted the 3rd Summit for Democracy in Seoul, focusing on 'Democracy for Future Generations' and AI impacts on electoral integrity.

questions.question: Which country officially legalized same-sex marriage in March 2026, becoming the first Southeast Asian nation to do so?
questions.explanation: The Thai Senate overwhelmingly passed the marriage equality bill, making Thailand the third jurisdiction in Asia (after Taiwan and Nepal) to legalize same-sex marriage.

questions.question: Which country became the newest member of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) in early 2024?
questions.explanation: Panama ratified the ISA Framework Agreement, with ISA membership expanding rapidly to over 100 full ratified member states globally.

questions.question: Where are the interim/permanent headquarters of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) located?
options: National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE) campus, Gurugram, Haryana, India
questions.explanation: ISA, launched jointly by India and France at COP21 in Paris, is the first international treaty-based intergovernmental organization headquartered in India (Gurugram).

questions.question: Who is the Director General of the International Solar Alliance (ISA)?
questions.explanation: Dr. Ajay Mathur led the ISA Secretariat, followed by leadership transitions overseen by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

questions.question: What is the visionary global initiative promoted by India through the ISA to create an interconnected green power grid?
options: OSOWOG (One Sun One World One Grid)
questions.explanation: OSOWOG aims to interconnect regional electrical grids across continents so that 'The Sun Never Sets' on clean renewable energy production.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), launched by India at the UN Climate Action Summit?
questions.explanation: CDRI is an international coalition headquartered in New Delhi, focusing on climate-resilient roads, telecom, and power systems in developing nations.

questions.question: Which country's capital hosted the ASEAN-India Senior Officials' Meeting (AISOM) in March 2026?
questions.explanation: Laos, holding the ASEAN Chairmanship for 2024, hosted high-level ASEAN-India meetings in its capital Vientiane.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) located?
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Secretariat is situated in Jakarta, Indonesia. ASEAN was founded in August 1967 with the Bangkok Declaration.

questions.question: How many member countries currently constitute ASEAN, with which nation slated as its 11th member?
options: 10 members, with Timor-Leste admitted in principle as the 11th member
questions.explanation: ASEAN has 10 members: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam; Timor-Leste holds observer status progressing toward full membership.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) located?
questions.explanation: The BIMSTEC Permanent Secretariat was established in Dhaka, Bangladesh, in 2014.

questions.question: How many member states constitute BIMSTEC?
options: 7 member states (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand)
questions.explanation: BIMSTEC brings together five South Asian nations (India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka) and two Southeast Asian nations (Myanmar, Thailand).

questions.question: In which year was BIMSTEC established through the Bangkok Declaration?
questions.explanation: BIMSTEC was founded in 1997 initially as BIST-EC (Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand Economic Cooperation), expanding later to include Myanmar, Nepal, and Bhutan.

questions.question: Which country held the Chairmanship of BIMSTEC leading up to the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in 2024-2026?
questions.explanation: Thailand held the Chair of BIMSTEC, hosting ministerial and leaders' conclaves in Bangkok under the theme 'Prosperous, Resilient and Open BIMSTEC'.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) located?
questions.explanation: The SAARC Secretariat was set up in Kathmandu on January 16, 1987. SAARC was founded in Dhaka in 1985.

questions.question: How many member countries are there in SAARC?
options: 8 countries (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka)
questions.explanation: SAARC comprises 8 member nations, with Afghanistan joining as the eighth member at the 14th SAARC Summit in New Delhi in 2007.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Secretariat located?
questions.explanation: The permanent Secretariat of the SCO is located in Beijing, China, while its counter-terrorism body RATS is in Tashkent.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) of the SCO situated?
questions.explanation: Executive Committee of SCO RATS is a permanent body based in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, coordinating intelligence-sharing on terrorism, separatism, and extremism.

questions.question: Which country officially joined as the 10th full member state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in 2024?
questions.explanation: Belarus officially joined the SCO as its 10th member state at the Astana Summit in July 2024, following Iran's induction as the 9th member in 2023.

questions.question: In which year did India and Pakistan formally become full members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
questions.explanation: India and Pakistan were formally inducted as full members of the SCO during the historical Astana Summit in Kazakhstan in June 2017.

questions.question: Which country hosted the SCO Defence Ministers Meeting in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan held the 2024 rotating Presidency of the SCO and hosted the Defence Ministers and Foreign Ministers in Astana.

questions.question: What magnitude earthquake struck Hualien County on Taiwan's eastern coast in April 2026, triggering international search & rescue responses?
questions.explanation: A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck Hualien, Taiwan's strongest quake in 25 years, with strict seismic building codes keeping casualties remarkably low.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) situated?
questions.explanation: The IAEA ('Atoms for Peace and Development') is headquartered at the Vienna International Centre in Austria.

questions.question: Who is the Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
questions.explanation: Argentine diplomat Rafael Mariano Grossi has served as Director General of the IAEA since 2019.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) located?
questions.explanation: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960 and relocated its headquarters to Vienna, Austria in 1965 (even though Austria is not an OPEC member).

questions.question: Which African oil-producing nation officially announced its withdrawal from OPEC in early 2024 following disagreements over output quotas?
questions.explanation: Angola exited OPEC after 16 years of membership, rejecting production quota cuts imposed by the cartel.

questions.question: What does 'OPEC+' denote in global energy markets?
options: OPEC member countries plus 10 non-OPEC oil producing nations led by Russia
questions.explanation: OPEC+ was formed in late 2016 by 12 OPEC members and 10 non-OPEC allies (including Russia, Kazakhstan, Oman, and Mexico) to coordinate oil supply.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the International Energy Agency (IEA) located?
questions.explanation: The IEA was created in 1974 within the OECD framework following the 1973 oil crisis and is headquartered in Paris.

questions.question: What is India's formal association status with the International Energy Agency (IEA)?
options: Association Country (since 2017, with talks underway for full membership)
questions.explanation: India became an Associate Member of the IEA in March 2017 and entered formal discussions for full membership in 2023-2024.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) situated?
questions.explanation: The IMO, the specialized UN agency responsible for the safety of shipping and marine pollution prevention, is headquartered in London along the River Thames.

questions.question: Who is the Secretary-General of the International Maritime Organization (IMO)?
questions.explanation: Arsenio Dominguez of Panama assumed office as the Secretary-General of the IMO on January 1, 2024.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) located?
questions.explanation: ICAO was established by the 1944 Chicago Convention on International Civil Aviation and has its headquarters in Montreal, Quebec, Canada.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Universal Postal Union (UPU) located?
questions.explanation: The Universal Postal Union, established by the Treaty of Bern in 1874, is the second oldest international organization and is based in Bern.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) located?
questions.explanation: The ITU, founded in 1865 as the International Telegraph Union, is the oldest UN specialized agency, headquartered in Geneva.

questions.question: Where did the ITU open its Area Office and Innovation Centre in South Asia in 2023?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the new ITU Area Office and Innovation Centre for South Asia at the MeitY complex in New Delhi.

questions.question: What is the 'Global Digital Compact' adopted by the United Nations Summit of the Future in 2024?
options: A comprehensive UN framework for open, free, secure, and human-centred digital cooperation and AI governance
questions.explanation: The Global Digital Compact establishes shared principles for universal internet access, digital public goods, data protection, and responsible artificial intelligence.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 77th/79th World Health Assembly (WHA) in May 2026 under the World Health Organization?
questions.explanation: The World Health Assembly, the supreme decision-making body of the WHO, meets annually at the Palais des Nations in Geneva.

questions.question: Who is the Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)?
questions.explanation: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus was first elected Director-General in 2017 and was re-elected for a second 5-year term in 2022.

questions.question: Where was the WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine (GCTM) established in 2022 under an agreement between India and WHO?
questions.explanation: The WHO GCTM is the world's first and only global outpost center for traditional medicine, established in Jamnagar, Gujarat.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 57th/59th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The ADB Annual Meeting was held in Tbilisi, Georgia, under the theme 'Bridge to the Future', focusing on climate finance and regional connectivity.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) located?
questions.explanation: The Asian Development Bank, established in 1966, is headquartered in Metro Manila, Philippines.

questions.question: Who is the President of the Asian Development Bank (ADB)?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) located?

questions.question: Who is the President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB)?

questions.question: Who is the current President of the New Development Bank (NDB / BRICS Bank)?

questions.question: Who served as the inaugural first President of the New Development Bank (NDB) from 2015 to 2020?

questions.question: Which country joined as a new member of the New Development Bank (NDB) in 2023-2024?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the International Labour Organization (ILO) located?

questions.question: Who is the Director-General of the International Labour Organization (ILO)?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) located?

questions.question: Who is the Director-General of UNESCO?

questions.question: How many World Heritage Sites from India are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as of mid-2026?
options: 43 sites (following the inclusion of Moidams of Assam)

questions.question: Which site from India was inscribed as India's 43rd UNESCO World Heritage Site at the 46th World Heritage Committee session in New Delhi?
options: Moidams – the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty, Charaideo, Assam
questions.explanation: The Royal Burial Mounds of the Ahom kings at Charaideo in Assam became the 43rd Indian property and the first cultural site from the Northeast on the UNESCO List.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 46th session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee in July 2024, the first time India hosted the prestigious event?
questions.explanation: India hosted the 46th Session of the World Heritage Committee for the first time at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.

questions.question: Which Indian sites were inscribed as the 41st and 42nd World Heritage Sites in September 2023?
options: Santiniketan (West Bengal) and Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (Karnataka)
questions.explanation: Santiniketan founded by Rabindranath Tagore was inscribed as the 41st site, and the 12th-century Hoysala temples (Belur, Halebid, Somnathapura) as the 42nd site.

questions.question: Which is India's only 'Mixed' (cultural and natural) UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation: Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim was inscribed in 2016 as India's sole Mixed World Heritage site.

questions.question: Which was the first site from India to be inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1983?
options: Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort, and Taj Mahal
questions.explanation: The initial batch of four Indian sites inscribed in 1983 were Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort, and the Taj Mahal.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) located?
questions.explanation: The FAO, a specialized agency of the UN leading international efforts to defeat hunger, was founded in 1945 in Quebec and relocated to Rome in 1951.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the World Food Programme (WFP), which won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020?
questions.explanation: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), the world's largest humanitarian agency addressing hunger and food security, is headquartered in Rome, Italy.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 50th/52nd G7 Summit held at the luxury resort of Borgo Egnazia in Apulia in June 2026?

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi participated in the G7 Outreach Session in Italy, delivering keynote remarks on which two key focus areas?
options: Artificial Intelligence & Energy, Africa and the Mediterranean
questions.explanation: PM Modi highlighted India's human-centric approach to AI ('AI for All') and energy transition during the G7 Outreach sessions.

questions.question: How many countries constitute the Group of Seven (G7)?
options: 7 countries (USA, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada) plus the European Union
questions.explanation: The G7 comprises the world's seven leading advanced industrial democracies: United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and Canada, with the EU as a non-enumerated member.

questions.question: Which country hosted the BRICS Foreign Ministers Meeting in June 2026?
questions.explanation: Russia held the 2024 BRICS Chairmanship under the motto 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Equitable Global Development and Security' and hosted the ministerial in Nizhny Novgorod.

questions.question: Which five new countries officially joined the BRICS grouping as full members on January 1, 2024?
options: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE)
Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Myanmar

questions.question: Which country hosted the 'Summit on Peace in Ukraine' at the Bürgenstock resort in June 2026?

questions.question: Who represented the Government of India at the Swiss Summit on Peace in Ukraine?

questions.question: Who is the Minister of External Affairs (MEA) of India?

questions.question: Who was appointed as the new Foreign Secretary of India in mid-2026, succeeding Vinay Mohan Kwatra?
questions.explanation: Veteran diplomat Vikram Misri (former Ambassador to China and Deputy NSA) took charge as the Foreign Secretary of India in July 2024.

questions.question: Where was Vinay Mohan Kwatra appointed after superannuating as India's Foreign Secretary?
options: Ambassador of India to the United States

questions.question: Who was appointed as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York in 2024, succeeding Ruchira Kamboj?
questions.explanation: Senior diplomat Parvathaneni Harish (former Ambassador to Germany) was appointed as India's Permanent Representative to the UN in New York.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the International Court of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) located?
questions.explanation: The ICC International Court of Arbitration, the world's leading commercial dispute resolution institution, is headquartered in Paris.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) situated?
questions.explanation: The PCA, established in 1899 by the First Hague Peace Conference, is the oldest global dispute resolution institution, based at the Peace Palace in The Hague.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF)?
options: Global money laundering and terrorist financing watchdog
questions.explanation: The FATF is an intergovernmental policymaking body that sets international standards to prevent money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) located?
questions.explanation: The FATF Secretariat is housed at the headquarters of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) in Paris.

questions.question: In its mutual evaluation report released in mid-2024/2026, which rating category did the FATF award to India for its anti-money laundering framework?
options: 'Regular Follow-up' category (the highest tier of technical compliance, alongside UK, France, and Italy)
questions.explanation: The FATF Plenary placed India in the coveted 'Regular Follow-up' category, commending India's measures in tackling illicit financial flows and terrorist financing.

questions.question: What does the 'Grey List' of the FATF formally signify for a listed jurisdiction?
options: Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring working with the FATF to address strategic deficiencies
High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to Call for Action
questions.explanation: Countries on the FATF 'Grey List' (officially 'Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring') commit to resolving deficiencies within agreed timeframes.

questions.question: What does the 'Black List' of the FATF signify, and which countries are currently on it?
options: High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action (currently North Korea, Iran, and Myanmar)
Nations in default of World Bank loans
questions.explanation: The FATF Black List comprises jurisdictions with significant strategic deficiencies; currently, Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), Iran, and Myanmar are blacklisted.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) located?
questions.explanation: The OECD, an intergovernmental organization of 38 high-income market economies, is based at Chateau de la Muette in Paris.

questions.question: Who is the Secretary-General of the OECD?
questions.explanation: Mathias Cormann, former Australian Finance Minister, assumed office as the Secretary-General of the OECD in June 2021.

questions.question: Which multilateral export control regime controls the transfer of conventional arms and dual-use goods and technologies, with India as its 42nd member?

questions.question: Which export control regime controls exports of chemical and biological agents and dual-use equipment, with India as its 43rd member?
questions.explanation: The Australia Group admitted India as its 43rd member in January 2018, reaffirming India's non-proliferation credentials.

questions.question: Which export control regime regulates the proliferation of missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles capable of carrying a 500 kg payload to at least 300 km?
questions.explanation: MTCR was established in 1987; India joined as its 35th member in June 2016, enabling extended-range BrahMos testing and drone exports.

questions.question: Which of the four major multilateral export control regimes has India NOT yet gained membership of, due to lack of consensus?
questions.explanation: India is a member of MTCR, Wassenaar Arrangement, and Australia Group, but its membership bid for the 48-nation NSG remains blocked by China due to NPT non-signatory criteria.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) located?
questions.explanation: UNEP is the leading global environmental authority within the UN system, founded in 1972 and based in Gigiri, Nairobi, Kenya.

questions.question: Which city hosted the 24th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in July 2026?

questions.question: Who represented India at the 24th SCO Summit in Astana?

questions.question: Which country officially assumed the rotating Presidency of the SCO for 2024-2025 at the conclusion of the Astana Summit?
questions.explanation: China took over the rotating SCO Presidency for 2024-2025 following Kazakhstan's successful tenure.

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi undertook a historic bilateral visit to Moscow in July 2026. What was the occasion?

questions.question: Which highest civilian honour of the Russian Federation was officially conferred upon Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his visit to Moscow?

questions.question: Following his visit to Russia, Prime Minister Modi visited which European country, marking the first visit by an Indian Prime Minister in 41 years since Indira Gandhi in 1983?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) located?

questions.question: Where was the 57th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting (AMM) and Post-Ministerial Conferences held in July 2026?

questions.question: Which country took over the rotating presidency of the Council of the European Union for the second half of 2024 from Belgium?

questions.question: Who is the President of the European Commission, re-elected for a second 5-year term in July 2026?

questions.question: Who is the President of the European Parliament, re-elected in July 2026?

questions.question: Who was chosen by EU leaders to succeed Charles Michel as the President of the European Council?

questions.question: Who was designated as the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, succeeding Josep Borrell?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the European Investment Bank (EIB) located?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the European Central Bank (ECB) situated?
questions.explanation: The European Central Bank, responsible for administering monetary policy of the Eurozone, has its seat in Frankfurt, Germany.

questions.question: Who is the President of the European Central Bank (ECB)?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), often referred to as the 'central bank for central banks'?

questions.question: Who serves as the General Manager of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS)?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the International Organization for Migration (IOM) located?

questions.question: Who is the Director General of the International Organization for Migration (IOM)?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) located?

questions.question: Who is the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) situated?

questions.question: India virtually hosted the 3rd 'Voice of Global South Summit' in August 2026. What was the overarching theme of the summit?

Unity of Voice, Unity of Purpose

questions.question: What initiative was proposed by India at the 3rd Voice of Global South Summit to build medical and healthcare resilience?

questions.question: Which country did Prime Minister Narendra Modi visit in August 2026, marking the first visit by an Indian Prime Minister to that nation in 45 years?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Modi visited Warsaw, Poland, holding bilateral talks with Prime Minister Donald Tusk, elevating bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership.

questions.question: What four bilateral agreements/MoUs were signed between India and Ukraine during the historic August 2026 visit?

questions.question: Where was the 18th East Asia Summit (EAS) senior officials meeting held in August 2026?

questions.question: How many member countries comprise the East Asia Summit (EAS)?
options: 18 countries (10 ASEAN nations + Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia, USA)

questions.question: Which city hosted the India-Japan 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue in August 2026?

Two trade ministers and two finance ministers

questions.question: Who is the Prime Minister of Japan who announced in August 2024 that he would step down?

questions.question: Who was appointed as the interim Chief Adviser of the Interim Government of Bangladesh in August 2024 following the resignation of Sheikh Hasina?
options: Nobel Peace Laureate Dr. Muhammad Yunus

questions.question: Which country hosted the Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) Leaders Meeting in August 2026?

questions.question: Where was the Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC) III Summit hosted by India in May 2023?

questions.question: What is the highest civilian honour of Papua New Guinea conferred on Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the FIPIC summit?

Companion of the Order of Fiji
Order of the Star of Melanesia

questions.question: What is the highest honour of Fiji conferred upon Prime Minister Narendra Modi?

questions.question: Which African nation conferred its highest national honour, 'The Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger' (GCON), on Prime Minister Modi in 2024?

questions.question: Which Caribbean nation conferred its highest civilian honour, 'The Order of Excellence', on Prime Minister Modi in 2024?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) located?

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) located?

questions.question: On which date is World Humanitarian Day observed globally each year to honour humanitarian aid workers?

questions.question: On which date is International Youth Day observed by the United Nations annually?

questions.question: On which date is National Youth Day celebrated in India to commemorate the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda?

questions.question: Which day is designated by the United Nations as the 'International Day against Nuclear Tests'?

questions.question: The Government of India conferred the highest civilian award 'Bharat Ratna' on how many eminent personalities in 2024?

questions.question: Who is revered as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India' who was posthumously conferred the Bharat Ratna?
questions.explanation: Dr. Mankombu Sambasivan Swaminathan led the development and introduction of high-yielding semi-dwarf wheat and rice varieties in India in the 1960s.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of the White Revolution' (Operation Flood) in India?
questions.explanation: Dr. Verghese Kurien ('Milkman of India') engineered Operation Flood, transforming India from a milk-deficient nation into the world's largest milk producer.

questions.question: Former Chief Minister of Bihar known affectionately as 'Jananayak' who was conferred the Bharat Ratna posthumously is:
questions.explanation: Karpoori Thakur was a socialist leader who championed social justice, reservation for backward classes, and land reforms in Bihar.

questions.question: Which former Prime Minister of India who served as the 9th Prime Minister from 1991 to 1996 and initiated economic liberalization was conferred the Bharat Ratna?

questions.question: Which former Prime Minister of India celebrated as a champion of farmers and the agrarian community was conferred the Bharat Ratna?

questions.question: On which date is National Farmers' Day (Kisan Diwas) celebrated annually in India?

questions.question: How many Padma Awards were conferred by the President of India on Republic Day (including Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri)?

questions.question: Founder of Sulabh International who was posthumously conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 2024 for social work and sanitation is:

questions.question: Renowned classical Bharatanatyam dancer and scholar who was conferred the Padma Vibhushan is:

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred the 'Order of St. Andrew the Apostle the First-Called' in Moscow in July 2026. What is the significance of this honour?
options: The highest state decoration and order of chivalry of the Russian Federation
questions.explanation: Established by Tsar Peter the Great in 1698, the Order of St. Andrew is Russia's highest decoration, conferred on PM Modi for developing special strategic partnership.

questions.question: How many foreign state honours and highest civilian decorations has Prime Minister Narendra Modi received from foreign nations as of mid-2026?
options: 15+ highest civilian awards from foreign nations
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Modi has been conferred highest state honours by over 15 nations, including Russia, France, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Afghanistan, Bahrain, Bhutan, Greece, and Nigeria.

questions.question: Which is the highest civilian award of France, conferred upon Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his visit as Chief Guest for Bastille Day?
options: Grand Cross of the Legion of Honour (Grand-Croix de la Légion d'Honneur)
questions.explanation: French President Emmanuel Macron bestowed the Grand Cross of the Legion of Honour—France's highest military and civilian order—upon PM Modi in Paris.

questions.question: Which is the highest civilian honour of Egypt, presented to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Cairo by President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi?
options: Order of the Nile (Collar of the Nile)
questions.explanation: President El-Sisi conferred Egypt's highest state decoration, the Collar of the Nile, on PM Modi during his landmark state visit to Cairo.

questions.question: Which is the highest civilian decoration of Greece, conferred upon Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Athens?
options: Grand Cross of the Order of Honour
questions.explanation: Greek President Katerina Sakellaropoulou bestowed the Grand Cross of the Order of Honour upon Prime Minister Modi in Athens.

questions.question: Who is the Chief Justice of India (CJI) serving in 2024-2026, succeeding Justice D.Y. Chandrachud?
questions.explanation: Justice Sanjiv Khanna was appointed as the 51st Chief Justice of India upon the superannuation of the 50th CJI, Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, on November 10, 2024.

questions.question: Who served as the 50th Chief Justice of India for a pivotal two-year tenure from November 2022 to November 2024?
questions.explanation: Justice D.Y. Chandrachud served as the 50th CJI, authoring historic verdicts on digital courts, Article 370 revocation validity, electoral bonds, and marriage equality.

questions.question: Who is scheduled in seniority to become the 52nd Chief Justice of India in May 2025?
questions.explanation: Justice B.R. Gavai is in line of succession to become the second Dalit Chief Justice of India after Justice K.G. Balakrishnan.

questions.question: Who is slated to become the first woman Chief Justice of India in September 2027?
questions.explanation: Justice B.V. Nagarathna of the Supreme Court of India is in line to become the nation's first female Chief Justice of India in September 2027.

questions.question: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India, appointed in 1989?
questions.explanation: Justice M. Fathima Beevi was appointed as the first female judge of the Supreme Court of India on October 6, 1989, later serving as Governor of Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Who was the first Chief Justice of independent India under the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Justice H.J. Kania took the oath of office as the first Chief Justice of India on January 26, 1950, when the Supreme Court came into existence.

questions.question: Who held the longest tenure as Chief Justice of India, serving for over seven years from 1978 to 1985?
questions.explanation: Justice Y.V. Chandrachud served as the 16th CJI for 7 years and 139 days (from February 1978 to July 1985), the longest in Indian judicial history.

questions.question: Who held the shortest tenure as Chief Justice of India, serving for just 17 days in 1991?
questions.explanation: Justice K.N. Singh served as the 22nd CJI for exactly 17 days (from November 25, 1991 to December 12, 1991).

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of Public Interest Litigation (PIL)' in India along with Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer?
questions.explanation: Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer pioneered Public Interest Litigation (epistolary jurisdiction) to give marginalized citizens access to justice.

questions.question: Which legendary Supreme Court judge delivered the lone dissenting judgment in the ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (Habeas Corpus case) during the Emergency?
questions.explanation: Justice H.R. Khanna courageously ruled that the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency, sacrificing his seniority for CJI.

questions.question: Who is the Attorney General for India, the highest law officer in the country under Article 76?
questions.explanation: Senior advocate R. Venkataramani was appointed as the 16th Attorney General for India in October 2022.

questions.question: Who is the Solicitor General of India, the second highest law officer of the country?
questions.explanation: Senior advocate Tushar Mehta has served as the Solicitor General of India since October 2018, receiving multiple tenure extensions.

questions.question: What unique right does the Attorney General for India have in Parliament under Article 88 of the Constitution?
options: The right to speak in and participate in proceedings of either House of Parliament or joint sittings, but without the right to vote
Full voting rights in Lok Sabha
Right to preside over Rajya Sabha
questions.explanation: Under Article 88, the Attorney General can speak and take part in proceedings of both Houses and parliamentary committees, but does not possess the right to cast a vote.

questions.question: What qualifications are required under Article 76(1) to be appointed as the Attorney General for India?
options: A person qualified to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: The President appoints a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court (citizen of India, High Court judge for 5 years or HC advocate for 10 years, or eminent jurist).

questions.question: What is the tenure of the Attorney General for India specified in the Constitution?
options: Holds office during the pleasure of the President (no fixed constitutional term)
questions.explanation: Article 76(4) specifies that the Attorney General shall hold office during the pleasure of the President and receive such remuneration as the President may determine.

questions.question: Who was the first Attorney General for independent India, holding office for a record 13 years from 1950 to 1963?
questions.explanation: M.C. Setalvad was India's first and longest-serving Attorney General, and also served as the first Chairman of the Law Commission of independent India.

questions.question: Who is the Chairman of the National Medical Commission (NMC), the apex regulator for medical education in India?
questions.explanation: Former NIMHANS Director Dr. B.N. Gangadhar was appointed as the Chairperson of the National Medical Commission, which replaced the Medical Council of India (MCI).

questions.question: Who is the Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and Secretary, Department of Health Research?
questions.explanation: Distinguished public health scientist Dr. Rajiv Bahl serves as the Director General of ICMR, headquartered at Ansari Nagar, New Delhi.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) located?
questions.explanation: ICMR, founded in 1911 as the Indian Research Fund Association (IRFA), is one of the oldest biomedical research bodies in the world, based in New Delhi.

questions.question: Where is the National Institute of Virology (NIV), a premier ICMR laboratory specializing in viral research and vaccine development, located?
questions.explanation: ICMR-NIV in Pune played a historic role in isolating the SARS-CoV-2 virus and co-developing India's indigenous Covid vaccine 'Covaxin' with Bharat Biotech.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the new Cabinet Secretary of India in August 2026, succeeding Rajiv Gauba after his record five-year tenure?
questions.explanation: Dr. T.V. Somanathan (1987 batch Tamil Nadu cadre IAS officer) was appointed as the Cabinet Secretary of India, the top-most civil servant in the Government of India.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Union Home Secretary in August 2026, succeeding Ajay Kumar Bhalla?
questions.explanation: Govind Mohan (1989 batch Sikkim cadre IAS officer, former Culture Secretary) took charge as the Union Home Secretary in the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in August 2024, succeeding Dr. Manoj Soni?
questions.explanation: Former Union Health Secretary Preeti Sudan (1983 batch Andhra Pradesh cadre IAS officer) was appointed by the President as the Chairperson of the UPSC.

questions.question: The President of India presented the inaugural 'Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar' awards at Rashtrapati Bhavan on National Space Day in August 2026. Who was conferred the prestigious 'Vigyan Ratna' (the lifetime achievement award in science)?
options: Prof. Govindarajan Padmanabhan (former Director of IISc Bengaluru)
questions.explanation: Eminent biochemist and pioneer of malaria parasite molecular biology Prof. G. Padmanabhan received the premier 'Vigyan Ratna' award from President Droupadi Murmu.

questions.question: How many categories comprise the unified 'Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar' instituted by the Government of India to replace legacy science awards?
options: 4 categories: Vigyan Ratna, Vigyan Shri, Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar, and Vigyan Team
questions.explanation: The Government consolidated dozens of science prizes into four prestigious tiers: Vigyan Ratna (lifetime), Vigyan Shri (distinguished contribution), Vigyan Yuva-SSB (under 45 years), and Vigyan Team (collaborative breakthroughs).

questions.question: Which landmark mission was conferred the 'Vigyan Team' award at the inaugural Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar ceremony?
questions.explanation: The ISRO Chandrayaan-3 team was honoured with the Vigyan Team award for accomplishing India's historic soft landing near the lunar south pole.

questions.question: Who was awarded the prestigious Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award, India's highest sporting honour, announced in the National Sports Awards?
options: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty (Badminton duo)
questions.explanation: Dynamic men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty received the Khel Ratna for their sensational triumphs at the Asian Games, Asian Championships, and Indonesia Open.

questions.question: What is the cash prize awarded to recipients of the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award?
options: ₹25 lakh, a medal, and a citation
questions.explanation: The Khel Ratna award carries a cash prize of ₹25 lakh (enhanced from ₹7.5 lakh in 2020), making it the highest monetary sports honour in India.

questions.question: In which year was the 'Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award' officially renamed as the 'Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award'?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the renaming of the Khel Ratna on August 6, 2021, in honor of hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand.

questions.question: Who was the very first recipient of the Khel Ratna Award in 1991-92?
questions.explanation: India's first chess Grandmaster and five-time World Chess Champion Viswanathan Anand was the inaugural winner of the Khel Ratna in 1991-92.

questions.question: Who was the first woman athlete to receive the Khel Ratna Award in 1994-95?
questions.explanation: Olympic bronze medallist weightlifter Karnam Malleswari was the first female recipient of the prestigious award.

questions.question: What is the cash prize awarded to recipients of the 'Arjuna Award' for outstanding performance in sports and games?
options: ₹15 lakh, a bronze statuette of Arjuna, and a citation
questions.explanation: The Arjuna Award carries a cash prize of ₹15 lakh, a bronze statuette of Arjuna, and a scroll of honour.

questions.question: Which award is conferred annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to recognize outstanding coaches in sports?
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award, instituted in 1985, honors coaches who have consistently enabled athletes to excel at international championships.

questions.question: What is the cash prize awarded for the Dronacharya Award in the Lifetime category?
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award Lifetime category carries a cash purse of ₹15 lakh, while the Regular category carries ₹10 lakh.

questions.question: Which award recognizes lifetime contribution to sports development and post-retirement dedication by veteran sportspersons?
options: Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime Achievement in Sports and Games
questions.explanation: Instituted in 2002, the Dhyan Chand Award honors sportspersons who have contributed to sports during their active career and continue to promote sports after retirement.

questions.question: What is the highest civilian award in India, instituted in 1954?
questions.explanation: Bharat Ratna, instituted on January 2, 1954, is the highest civilian award of the Republic of India, awarded for exceptional service/performance of the highest order.

questions.question: Who were the first three recipients of the Bharat Ratna in 1954?
options: C. Rajagopalachari, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, and Dr. C.V. Raman
Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Patel, and Rajendra Prasad
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Bhagwan Das, and M. Visvesvaraya
Govind Ballabh Pant, DK Karve, and BC Roy
questions.explanation: The first Bharat Ratna awards were conferred upon the last Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari, philosopher-statesman Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, and Nobel laureate physicist Dr. C.V. Raman.

questions.question: Who was the first person to be posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1966?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri was the first person to be honoured posthumously with the Bharat Ratna following his sudden demise at Tashkent in 1966.

questions.question: Who was the first naturalized/foreign citizen to receive the Bharat Ratna in 1980?
questions.explanation: Mother Teresa (naturalized Indian citizen) received the Bharat Ratna in 1980, followed by foreign nationals Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987) and Nelson Mandela (1990).

questions.question: Who was the first non-Indian citizen without Indian citizenship to be awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1987?
questions.explanation: Pakistani national and legendary freedom fighter Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Badshah Khan) was the first non-citizen to be awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1987.

questions.question: Who is the youngest recipient of the Bharat Ratna, awarded at the age of 40 in 2014?
questions.explanation: Cricket icon Sachin Tendulkar became the youngest person and the first sportsperson to receive the Bharat Ratna in 2014.

questions.question: What is the design of the Bharat Ratna medallion?
options: A peepal-leaf shaped medallion in bronze with a platinum sun and 'Bharat Ratna' embossed in Devanagari
questions.explanation: The medallion is cast in bronze in the shape of a peepal leaf, with an embossed replica of the Sun in platinum on the obverse and the State Emblem of India on the reverse.

questions.question: Does the Bharat Ratna award carry any monetary cash grant?
options: No monetary grant is attached to the Bharat Ratna; it includes a Sanad (certificate signed by the President) and a medallion
questions.explanation: Unlike civilian gallantry or sports awards, no cash allowance is provided with the Bharat Ratna; recipients receive a presidential Sanad and a medallion, and figure 7th in the Table of Precedence.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of Bharat Ratna awards that can normally be conferred in a single calendar year under official regulations?
options: Three awards (though exceptional special relaxations occurred in 1999 and 2024)
questions.explanation: Statutory regulations restrict Bharat Ratna awards to a maximum of three in a calendar year, although the government made rare exceptions in 1999 (4 awards) and 2024 (5 awards).

questions.question: Which civilian decoration ranks immediately below the Bharat Ratna in the Indian honours system?
questions.explanation: The hierarchy of civilian honours is: 1. Bharat Ratna, 2. Padma Vibhushan (exceptional and distinguished service), 3. Padma Bhushan (distinguished service of high order), 4. Padma Shri (distinguished service).
